title.rendered: Yawkey Foundation supports patients and staff

content.rendered:
Winter 2023
By Kayla Carcone

In 1953, Tom and Jean Yawkey initiated what would become a legacy of remarkable support by helping to establish the historic relationship between the Boston Red Sox, Sidney Farber, MD, and the Jimmy Fund. Now, 70 years later, the Yawkey Foundation continues to forge meaningful connections while enhancing the daily experiences of our patients and staff, most recently awarding $100,000 to the Adult Patient Assistance Program at Dana-Farber.

This support helps to alleviate financial hardship for patients and families undergoing treatment at the Institute. Thanks in part to the generosity of the Yawkey Foundation, Deborah Toffler, MSW, LSCW, senior director of patient care services, and her team have an expanded capacity to assist patients with the cost of groceries, travel expenses, and other needs created by financial strain.

This gift also funded a staff appreciation event in August, which brought Cookie Monstah, an ice cream sandwich food truck, to the Yawkey Center for Cancer Care. “We are delighted that the power of this grant will be amplified through a gesture of appreciation, recognizing the many individual employees across various functions doing heroic work every day in cancer treatment and research,” said Maureen Bleday, CEO of the Yawkey Foundation.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Yawkey Foundation’s heartfelt support
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Yawkey Foundation is a longtime partner of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, stemming from the historic relationship between the Jimmy Fund and the Boston Red Sox. Perpetuating the philanthropic legacy of the team’s owners, Tom and Jean Yawkey, the foundation made gifts totaling $180,000 in 2024.

img.alt_text: Two people holding ice cream outside a Cookie Monstah food truck

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jimmy Fund Little League
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Jimmy Fund Little League presented by the Yawkey Foundation surpassed its $275,000 goal, contributing $359,476 of unrestricted funding to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and underscoring the Yawkey Foundation’s dedication to advancing care for its community. The top fundraising team was North Reading 10U Gold, raising $18,465, and the top individual fundraiser, James Keohan, raised $10,617.

title.rendered: Larry Lucchino receives Jimmy Fund’s highest honor

content.rendered:
Winter 2023
By Colleen Sullivan
Photography by Maddie Malhotra/Boston Red Sox

The 2023 Boston Red Sox Jimmy Fund Award was presented to Chairman of the Jimmy Fund Larry Lucchino at a special Fenway Park ceremony in August. The award is the Jimmy Fund’s highest honor, presented annually by the Red Sox to those who have demonstrated exceptional, longstanding commitment to the lifesaving mission of Dana-Farber and the Jimmy Fund.

“Working with the Jimmy Fund has been one of my greatest joys in life, and I’m looking forward to someday a Boston and a world without cancer.”

Larry Lucchino

Lucchino was appointed Chairman of the Jimmy Fund in 2016, and in this role he serves as lead ambassador and public spokesperson for the charity. But his involvement goes back much farther than that. For many years, Lucchino has been a supporter, advocate, Institute Trustee, and patient of Dana-Farber, all the while championing our mission. As Chairman/Principal Owner of the Worcester Red Sox and President/CEO Emeritus of the Boston Red Sox, Lucchino has been a passionate steward of the partnership between the Red Sox and the Jimmy Fund, which is the longest and most successful team-charity relationship in all of professional sports.

“I am incredibly honored and humbled to receive this year’s Boston Red Sox Jimmy Fund Award,” said Lucchino. “Working with the Jimmy Fund has been one of my greatest joys in life, and I’m looking forward to someday a Boston and a world without cancer.”

jetpack-related-posts.title: Larry Lucchino (1945 – 2024): Beloved Champion
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Dana-Farber and Jimmy Fund community mourn the passing of Larry Lucchino, longtime Institute Trustee and Chairman of the Jimmy Fund who died peacefully on April 2, 2024, surrounded by his loving family and friends.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Chairmen of the Jimmy Fund: building community since 1948
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Since the earliest days of the Jimmy Fund, passionate and committed individuals have devoted their time, talents, resources, and relationships to raising money in support of a powerful possibility: curing cancer for everyone.

img.alt_text: Larry Lucchino at the Boston Marathon Jimmy Fund Walk

jetpack-related-posts.title: Red Sox name 2023 Jimmy Fund Captain
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Boston Red Sox pitcher, Garrett Whitlock, has been named Jimmy Fund Captain for the 2023 baseball season.

img.alt_text: Jimmy Fund Captain Garrett Whitlock in the Fenway dugout with pediatric patient Lily

jetpack-related-posts.title: Meet the new Co-Chairs of the Jimmy Fund: Brock Holt and Tom Caron
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Holt and Caron will be the lead ambassadors and public spokespeople on behalf of the Jimmy Fund, helping to raise funds and awareness.

title.rendered: Bell & Hudson Putt-a-Thon surpasses $1 million raised

content.rendered:
Winter 2023
By Colleen Sullivan

The 19th Annual Bell & Hudson Putt-a-Thon for the Jimmy Fund celebrated a major milestone in surpassing $1 million raised since its inception.

It all started in 2005, when a group of employees from Bell & Hudson Insurance Agency came together to help those in their community affected by cancer. Held on the town common of Belchertown, Mass., the mini golf tournament now draws hundreds of people of all ages and has become a beloved event for the community.

“Almost 20 years later, we’ve raised more than $1 million for the Jimmy Fund,” said tournament director Jim Phaneuf. “This milestone was only possible due to the absolute dedication of a small team of volunteers, and the hundreds of mini golfers and donors who have opened up their wallets and hearts year after year.”

jetpack-related-posts.title: Meghan McCarthy Fund marks milestone
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Meghan McCarthy Research Fund surpassed $1 million in funding to support glioblastoma research at Dana-Farber in memory of a high school athlete and Jimmy Fund fundraiser who passed away in 2010.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Walkers go the extra mile for the Jimmy Fund
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The annual Awards and Milestones Reception recognized participants of the 2024 Jimmy Fund Walk presented by Hyundai who went above and beyond in helping to raise nearly $9.4 million.

img.alt_text: Five Jimmy Fund Walk participants wearing Jimmy Fund Walk gear

jetpack-related-posts.title: Walkers go the extra mile for the Jimmy Fund
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The annual Awards and Milestones Reception recognized participants of the 2023 Boston Marathon® Jimmy Fund Walk presented by Hyundai who went above and beyond.

img.alt_text: Zach’s Pack Jimmy Fund Walk fundraising group

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon breaks records with $5.7 million raised for Dana-Farber
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The WEEI/NESN Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon presented by Arbella Insurance continued to be a beacon of support for Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund in August with a record-breaking fundraising year.

img.alt_text: Ali Kelleher cheering at Fenway Park

jetpack-related-posts.title: Pan-Mass Challenge makes record-breaking $78 million gift to drive Dana-Farber’s progress against cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC), a bike-a-thon that raises more money for charity than any other single athletic fundraising event in the world, has built an unparalleled track record for success strengthened by touchstone traditions and continuous improvements in pursuit of the goal of defying cancer.

img.alt_text: A child holding a 'We love PMC riders' sign among a group of bike riders

jetpack-related-posts.title: Another ace year for Jimmy Fund Golf
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Jimmy Fund Golf presented by Mohegan Sun raised $6.8 million in 2024, thanks to organizers and participants in more than 140 events across the country.

title.rendered: Celebrating the Lunder Family Chair in Leukemia

content.rendered:
Winter 2023
By Nahshon Yisrael
Photography by Justin Knight

On June 29, colleagues, friends, and loved ones gathered in celebration of the Lunder Family Chair in Leukemia at Dana-Farber, established with a generous endowment by Paula and Peter Lunder and The Lunder Family Foundation. Richard Stone, MD, chief of staff and the director of translational research in the Division of Leukemia at Dana-Farber (pictured, third from left), is the chair’s inaugural incumbent, and the chair will be renamed for Stone upon his retirement. Pictured with Stone at the celebration are (from left): Kevin Gillis, president of The Lunder Family Foundation; Stone’s wife, Jane Brown, MD; Paula and Peter Lunder; and Dana-Farber President and CEO Laurie H. Glimcher, MD.

Stone, MD, the Lunder Family Chair in Leukemia at Dana-Farber. The gift will advance Stone’s research to identify novel targets in acute leukemia and myelodysplastic syndromes.

jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The CLL Global Research Foundation awarded generous grants totaling $600,000 to Dana-Farber, supporting the research of Catherine Wu, MD, Lavine Family Chair for Preventative Cancer Therapies, and Erin Parry, MD, PhD. content.rendered:
Winter 2023
By Lori Dougherty, Gabriella Medeiros, Holly Roman
Art and Photography by Grace Howard, Michael Blanchard

Our generous donor community is relentless and powerful in your commitment to our mission to defy cancer at every turn. In the past year you took the momentum of The Dana-Farber Campaign to a whole new level, ending the fiscal year on Sept. 30 with an amazing all-time high of $407.4 million raised, including a record $109.9 million for the Jimmy Fund. Thanks to gifts large and small—from philanthropic organizations and individuals, and hundreds of thousands of grassroots supporters across the nation and around the world—Dana- Farber has shepherded new treatments through FDA approval, expanded access to care for underserved communities, harnessed new technologies, improved early detection, and so much more. Thank you for advancing cancer research and patient care for patients and families everywhere.

FY23 Fundraising Results
For the fiscal year October 1, 2022 – September 30, 2023

Total Funds Raised
$407.4 million

Total Donors
228,863

Portion raised for the Jimmy Fund
$109.9 million

jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The success of our mission hinges on unrestricted gifts, including those raised through the Defy Cancer Fund.

jetpack-related-posts.author: danafarberandthejimmyfund@gmail.com
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Establishing an endowment is a powerful way to support The Dana-Farber Campaign.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Eisenson encourages CGAs as a simple and lasting legacy
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Supporting cancer research and care at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute can take many forms that benefit both the Institute and the donor. Michael Eisenson (pictured), Institute Trustee and chair of The Dana-Farber Campaign, recently established a charitable gift annuity (CGA) with a generous gift of $250,000.

img.alt_text: Michael Eisenson at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute's healing garden

jetpack-related-posts.title: Estate of Carolyn Brophy
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Estate of Carolyn Brophy has generously bequeathed $120,697.36 to support cancer research and care at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. Carolyn’s commitment to Dana-Farber’s mission will drive promising research and innovative treatments. Her legacy will inspire breakthroughs and improve patient experiences, helping Dana-Farber continue to defy cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Together in action, together in progress: Giving Day surpasses fundraising goal
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: This year’s annual Giving Day marked an especially generous occasion for dedicated supporters of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund.

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Message from Melany Duval
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dear friends, Every day our philanthropic community supports a relentless commitment to possibilities in cancer care at Dana-Farber—and that gives me hope.

content.rendered:
Winter 2023
By Kathy Clute
Photography by Sam Ogden

Ten years ago, Dana-Farber leaders created the Faculty Research Fund (FRF), a unique financing mechanism that pools philanthropic resources to accelerate bold scientific discovery. Each time a restricted gift is made—one directed to a specific project or program—10 percent of that gift is allocated to the FRF to support investments that ensure progress across all cancers.

In fiscal year 2023, Dana-Farber allocated more than $11 million to the FRF for institutional priorities that cut across disciplines and facilitate breakthroughs. Cumulatively, the FRF has deployed $66.2 million to advance our research mission since it was established in 2013.

Projects to receive funding via the FRF this year include the Center for Precision Immuno-Oncology (CPIO), which fosters collaborative, translational research among lab and clinical investigators in many disease centers. Physician-scientists from the CPIO developed the NeoVax vaccine that has been proven effective against advanced melanoma and is being tested in other cancers.

Meanwhile, the Center for Pediatric Cancer Therapeutics, which also received funds from the FRF, has achieved remarkable advances in epigenetics and genomics that are already helping children in the clinic. In addition, the FRF is funding a multiyear data curation project to make high-quality patient data across all cancer types more readily available for research studies.

None of this progress would be possible without our esteemed faculty members, who are among the world’s most exceptional researchers. Their dedication to scientific discovery and patient care routinely leads to paradigm-shifting approaches for diagnosing, preventing, treating, and curing cancer. The FRF makes it possible for Institute leaders to recruit and retain early career and senior faculty and to fill gaps in grant funding that would otherwise compromise projects with the potential to save and extend lives.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Faculty Research Fund sparks innovation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Faculty Research Fund supports Dana-Farber priorities that transcend individual disciplines and facilitate breakthroughs across all cancer types.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Philanthropic support advances faculty work
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Each day at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, faculty members work toward research breakthroughs, provide care and moments of hope to patients, and strive to go above and beyond in the fight against cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Message from Melany Duval
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: One of the things that makes Dana-Farber such a special place is our emphasis on teamwork.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Expect Miracles Foundation continues to drive discovery
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: For the 29th year, Expect Miracles Foundation reaffirmed their support of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute with a gift of $1 million.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Campaign
jetpack-related-posts.author: danafarberandthejimmyfund@gmail.com
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Establishing an endowment is a powerful way to support The Dana-Farber Campaign.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Expect Miracles Foundation invests $1.1 million to accelerate cancer breakthroughs at the Belfer Center
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: For more than 25 years, Expect Miracles Foundation has united leaders across the financial services industry and beyond to advance life-saving cancer research and support those impacted by the disease.

content.rendered:
Fall 2023

Dear Friends,

When Dr. Sidney Farber achieved the first remissions in childhood leukemia in 1947, he changed everything. His work sparked a new era of hope and possibility in cancer science and medicine and led to the launch of the Jimmy Fund in 1948. Seventy-five years later, the Jimmy Fund continues to support our clinicians and researchers as they stand on the shoulders of Dr. Farber, and strive to fulfill his vision from all those years ago of changing the field of cancer medicine.

Our generous donor community supports that legacy. Many of you give today, through contributions large and small, to ensure we have a strong foundation in the future. Many of you have included Dana-Farber in your estate plans, providing planned gifts that will fund the next big breakthrough decades from now. Many of you raise money by riding in the Pan-Mass Challenge, which just had its most successful ride ever in August, or by participating in other Dana-Farber and Jimmy Fund events in your community. Many of you share your stories, and in that way, you inspire others.

The Dana-Farber and Jimmy Fund community remains strong because of you. This year, as we celebrate the Jimmy Fund’s 75th anniversary together, all of us at Dana-Farber are looking forward to many more achievements, powered by your support, in the years to come.

With gratitude,

Melany N. Duval
Senior Vice President and Chief Philanthropy Officer

content.rendered:
Fall 2023
By Brittany Flaherty

The Dana-Farber Campaign is an ambitious, multi-year fundraising effort to change the future of cancer research and care—the largest in the Institute’s history and one of the largest ever in the U.S. focused solely on cancer. Our community of support is crucial to this effort.

One way our supporters accelerate campaign efforts is by including Dana-Farber in their estate plans. During the campaign, the Dana-Farber Society has grown by 70% to 1,750 members—approaching our goal to grow our legacy community to 2,000 members. Donors have made new planned giving commitments totaling more than $269 million to advance key science and care initiatives, establish endowed fellowships to attract the most innovative young minds, and provide flexible funds that allow the Institute to take risks in our science, seize key opportunities, and expand our reach.

Many times planned gifts provide tax advantages to the donor, while providing reliable future support for our most ambitious efforts to improve outcomes for adults and children with cancer here and around the world. Together, we can transform cancer care for patients everywhere.

To learn more, visit DefyCancer.org.

excerpt.rendered: One way our supporters accelerate campaign efforts is by including Dana-Farber in their estate plans.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Campaign
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Dana-Farber Campaign has inspired pivotal planned gifts that will make a true difference for children and adults with cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Campaign
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On Sept. 30, Dana-Farber announced the completion of one of the largest-ever fundraising campaigns focused solely on cancer: The Dana-Farber Campaign.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Campaign: Join Us
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With three months remaining in The Dana-Farber Campaign, there is still time to join us in this truly historic effort that will forever change cancer research and care.

img.alt_text: Dana-Farber Trustees Monica Chandra and Michael Eisenson in the hospital's healing garden

jetpack-related-posts.title: Palm Beach surpasses $67 million in gifts to The Dana-Farber Campaign
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: For over three decades, the compassionate community in Palm Beach, Florida, has provided generous support for Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s lifesaving mission to conquer cancer in adults and children—not only in Boston and Palm Beach, but also across the country and around the world.

img.alt_text: Dana-Farber Palm Beach Campaign Leadership Celebration Dinner

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Campaign
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber has played a critical role in the development of more than half of all cancer drugs approved by the FDA in the past 5 years.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Campaign Cabinet
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Campaign Cabinet devoted their time, talents, and resources to advancing The Dana-Farber Campaign’s mission to Defy Cancer.

content.rendered:
Fall 2023
By Lucy Klemarczyk

The American Association for Cancer Research (AACR) recently awarded $480,000 to four Dana-Farber physician-scientists who are investigating new methods of prevention, diagnosis, and treatment for various types of cancers. As the first cancer research organization dedicated to preventing and curing cancer, AACR is a long-standing partner in Dana-Farber’s mission to defy cancer.

Fall 2023
By Colleen Sullivan

The Glenn Foundation for Medical Research and the American Federation for Aging Research awarded a $300,000 grant to support basic science research by Dana-Farber’s Edward Chouchani, PhD, as he seeks to systematically define the functional targets of reactive oxygen species that contribute to longevity and age.

jetpack-related-posts.title: American Gastroenterological Association Research Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The American Gastroenterological Association Research Foundation's generous grant of $100,000 supports the research of Dana-Farber’s Harshabad (Harsh) Singh, MBBS. This funding empowers him to further explore the biological foundations of HER2-driven gastric tumors and test innovative therapies. This can potentially transform treatment approaches for this challenging disease.

This funding will support her work in treatment resistance in HER2+ breast cancer brain metastases and ultimately help transform the landscape of patient care.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Samuel Waxman Cancer Research Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Samuel Waxman Cancer Research Foundation awarded $200,000 to Dana-Farber to support research into how aging affects the behavior of tumor cells. This research, led by Lewis Cantley, PhD, in the Department of Cancer Biology, could provide further insight that may inform the development of age-specific treatment approaches for cancer.

content.rendered:
Fall 2023
By Katherine Agate

The B.A.A. 5K® took place April 15, welcoming the largest team to date of Dana-Farber runners who collectively raised $184,271. Runners had the option to race in person on the 3.1-mile course that began and ended in the Boston Common, or run in their own neighborhoods as virtual teammates. The top fundraiser honor went to David Mullen.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dana-Farber recruits largest B.A.A. Half Marathon® team to date
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The 2023 B.A.A. Half Marathon® was a race to remember, with 650 participants running Sunday, Nov. 12, to support Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s race toward a cancer-free future.

img.alt_text: A group photo of Dana-Farber runners at the BAA Half Marathon in 2023

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dana-Farber’s Boston half team sets new record
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Sunday, November 9, marked the Boston Athletic Association’s (B.A.A.’s) annual Boston Half, a scenic 13.1-mile race through Franklin Park and the Emerald Necklace Park System.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dana-Farber’s B.A.A. Half team runs 13.1 miles to defy cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The B.A.A. Half Marathon® returned to Boston’s Emerald Necklace on Sunday, Nov. 13, 2022, in person for the first time since 2019. Dana-Farber’s 2022 B.A.A. Half team included 485 team members running 13.1 miles, both in-person and virtually, to support Dana-Farber’s commitment to groundbreaking research and quality patient care.

jetpack-related-posts.title: A record-breaking year for Dana-Farber’s ASICS Falmouth Road Race team
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: This year, on August 17, runners from Dana-Farber’s 2025 Falmouth Road Race team raised a record-breaking $1,105,554.90, the highest fundraising total in the team’s 23-year history, which exceeds $12.5 million to date for innovative research and compassionate patient care.

img.alt_text: Falmouth Road Race team in Dana-Farber gear

jetpack-related-posts.title: Runners across the country race for Dana-Farber and the Jimmy Fund
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The 2022 Run Any Race season roster consisted of 71 runners, running various races across the globe in support of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund.

img.alt_text: Andrew Kaczysnki of Team Beans on the course

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dana-Farber team defies cancer in ASICS Falmouth Road Race
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On Aug. 21, more than 330 members of Dana-Farber’s team ran seven miles along the scenic Cape Cod coastline for the 50th running of the ASICS Falmouth Road Race.

img.alt_text: Falmouth Road Race Team Power runners

content.rendered:
Fall 2023
By Colleen Sullivan
Photography by Capehart Photography

Sandra Bornstein and her late husband, Richard, made a generous commitment of $400,000 to support early career physician-scientists on the leukemia and stem cell transplant teams at Dana-Farber. Faculty excellence is a top priority of  The Dana-Farber Campaign, and this funding will help fuel the growth of promising investigators as they work to ensure greater numbers of patients live longer, healthier lives.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Harold and Janice Cohen Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Harold and Janice Cohen Foundation made a generous $150,000 gift in support of lifelong friend Richard M. Stone, MD, the Lunder Family Chair in Leukemia at Dana-Farber. The gift will advance Stone’s research to identify novel targets in acute leukemia and myelodysplastic syndromes.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Wipe Out Kids’ Cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With a total contribution of more than $230,000, Wipe Out Kids’ Cancer is supporting two Dana-Farber researchers as they work to enhance treatment options for children with leukemia. One study aims to improve the recovery process for stem cell transplant patients, while the other is testing a new combination therapy…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Bill Pomeroy gives the gift of access to patients with blood cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: After his successful transplant, Pomeroy was inspired to help create better outcomes for patients like him. In 2005, he founded the William G. Pomeroy Foundation® to raise awareness and fund initiatives to improve access to blood cancer care. Pomeroy and his foundation have since made gifts totaling more than $1…

img.alt_text: Bill Pomeroy with William G. Pomeroy Foundation banners

jetpack-related-posts.title: Giving Day celebrates 75 years of progress
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On May 22, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund held its fourth annual Giving Day—an inspirational day of hope, where supporters come together as a community to raise critical funds to defy cancer.

img.alt_text: A pediatric cancer patient smiling and holding a cookie

jetpack-related-posts.title: Celebrating the Lunder Family Chair in Leukemia
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On June 29, colleagues, friends, and loved ones gathered in celebration of the Lunder Family Chair in Leukemia at Dana-Farber, established with a generous endowment by Paula and Peter Lunder and The Lunder Family Foundation.

img.alt_text: Group photo from the celebration of the Lunder Family Chair in Leukemia at Dana-Farber

jetpack-related-posts.title: Cure Childhood Cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s Emily Heikamp, MD, PhD, MSc, received a $220,000 Early Investigator Award from CURE Childhood Cancer. This generous grant supports her research focused on determining whether targeting two proteins can effectively treat a specific type of acute myeloid leukemia. Fall 2023
By Colleen Sullivan
Photography by Michael Blanchard

The Clifford Family established the Woolley-Clifford Foundation Fund with a $100,000 gift, supporting the research of David Kozono, MD, PhD, as he works to investigate blood and tissue-based biomarkers in lung cancer patients that can help predict lung inflammation and anti-tumor response following radiation therapy.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Mindy Green
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With a $100,000 gift, Mindy Green established the Li Li Family EGFR Lung Cancer Research Fund in memory of her mother, Li Li. The fund realizes Li Li’s intention to make a gift to Dana-Farber and will support the cutting-edge research of her thoracic oncologist, Michael Rabin, MD.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Joe Connolly
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Joe Connolly established the Deborah Connolly Small Cell Lung Cancer Research Fund at Dana-Farber in honor of his late wife, with a gift of $100,000. The fund will support research such as studies of the molecular mutations driving small cell lung cancer, with the goal of developing targeted therapies.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Joe Connolly
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Joe Connolly gave $100,000 to fund critical small cell lung cancer research at Dana-Farber. Established in honor of Connolly’s late wife, the Deborah A. Connolly Small Cell Lung Cancer Research Fund is supporting Jacob Sands, MD, who in collaboration with Matthew Oser, MD, PhD, is exploring new methods to predict…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Free ME from Lung Cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Free ME from Lung Cancer Research Fund doubled its impact, matching a previous gift of $100,000 to support research conducted by Jia Luo, MD, in Dana-Farber’s Lowe Center for Thoracic Oncology. The investment will fuel immunotherapy research for patients with an aggressive and underfunded type of lung cancer.

img.alt_text: Free ME from Lung Cancer Research Fund logo

jetpack-related-posts.title: Mugar Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Mugar Foundation made a generous commitment of $500,000 to support the previously established Mugar Family Fellowship in Lung Cancer. While advancing promising lung cancer research, the fellowship provides reliable funding for an early career scientist to pursue innovative research and develop the skills needed to lead the future of…

img.alt_text: Steaming beaker and pipette in the lab

jetpack-related-posts.title: Robinson Family
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Robinson Family established the memorial Lena Maximo Robinson Fund with a $100,000 gift, supporting the melanoma research of F. Stephen Hodi Jr., MD, the Sharon Crowley Martin Chair in Melanoma at Dana-Farber. With these funds, Hodi’s team will continue their leadership in developing next-generation, cutting-edge treatments for all subtypes…

Fall 2023
By Katherine Agate
Photography by Jessamyn Martin

The Harold and Janice Cohen Foundation made a generous $150,000 gift in support of lifelong friend Richard M. Stone, MD, the Lunder Family Chair in Leukemia at Dana-Farber. The gift will advance Stone’s research to identify novel targets in acute leukemia and myelodysplastic syndromes.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Celebrating the Lunder Family Chair in Leukemia
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On June 29, colleagues, friends, and loved ones gathered in celebration of the Lunder Family Chair in Leukemia at Dana-Farber, established with a generous endowment by Paula and Peter Lunder and The Lunder Family Foundation.

img.alt_text: Group photo from the celebration of the Lunder Family Chair in Leukemia at Dana-Farber

jetpack-related-posts.title: Rosenberg Family
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Rosenberg family has made a generous gift to support patients through all aspects of the breast cancer journey. Their gift funds triple-negative breast cancer research led by Elizabeth Mittendorf, MD, PhD, MHCM; research training led by Harold Burstein, MD, PhD; infusion nursing directed by Anne Gross, PhD, RN, NEA-BC,…

jetpack-related-posts.title: CLL Global Research Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The CLL Global Research Foundation awarded generous grants totaling $600,000 to Dana-Farber, supporting the research of Catherine Wu, MD, Lavine Family Chair for Preventative Cancer Therapies, and Erin Parry, MD, PhD. This funding will help advance their studies of chronic lymphocytic leukemia, aiming to uncover new insights and improve treatment…

jetpack-related-posts.title: High-risk, high-reward research is The Mathers Foundation’s priority
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Transformative basic research is the focus of The G. Harold and Leila Y. Mathers Charitable Foundation, which recently awarded $1.5 million to fund Dana-Farber research on unraveling the inner workings of human cells.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dienna and John Lehner
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dienna and John Lehner recommended a gift totaling $100,000 to the board of the Orchard Foundation, to support leukemia research under the direction of Dana-Farber researchers, Robert Soiffer, MD, and Daniel DeAngelo, MD, PhD.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Rheumatology Research Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A generous gift of $225,000 from the Rheumatology Research Foundation has been made to support Dana-Farber research fellow Michelle Robinette, MD, PhD. This gift will support Robinette as she continues her groundbreaking research in rheumatology, fostering innovation and improving patient care.

content.rendered:
Fall 2023
By Colleen Sullivan
Photography by Sam Ogden

The Colorectal Cancer Alliance made a $150,000 grant to Dana-Farber to fund research into new treatments for colorectal cancer, the third most common type of cancer worldwide. Building on previous research, a Dana-Farber team is working to develop a novel class of therapeutics designed to promote cancer cell death by inducing cancer cell maturation.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Rasmussen Family funds research into underlying causes of colorectal cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Anna and Neil Rasmussen are no strangers to medical research in the quest to find answers to chronic illness—one of their children had been living with ulcerative colitis since she was seven years old.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Russ Agrusa honors late wife by fueling colorectal cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Russ and his late wife, Paula, established the Project P Fund in 2014 with a goal of empowering researchers at Dana-Farber to develop more effective targeted and immune-based therapies for patients with colorectal cancer. Since Paula’s death in 2016, Russ has continued to honor her legacy through ongoing support for…

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Cox Family continues support of Dana-Farber’s revolutionary science
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Career venture capitalist and Institute Trustee Howard Cox and his wife, Wendy Cox, are no strangers to the revolutionary science and clinical treatments happening at the Institute.

jetpack-related-posts.title: V Foundation grants power colorectal cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The V Foundation for Cancer Research once again demonstrated its remarkable generosity and commitment to advancing cancer research at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute by awarding $1.4 million in grants to two exceptional investigators.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Alison Poorvu Jaffe and Dan Jaffe support Young-Onset Colorectal Cancer Center
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Alison Poorvu Jaffe and her husband, Dan Jaffe, renewed their support for the Young-Onset Colorectal Cancer Center at Dana-Farber to help stem the disease’s dramatic rise among people under 50.

img.alt_text: Two people pose for a photo at Fenway Park

jetpack-related-posts.title: David Rathburn
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With a generous $150,000 gift, David Rathburn (pictured), through the Rathburn Family Foundation, supported a clinical trial led by Dana-Farber’s Benjamin Schlechter, MD. The clinical trial aims to expand the benefits of immunotherapy to more colorectal cancer patients, with a specific focus on reducing unwanted side effects of these therapies.

content.rendered:
Fall 2023
By Colleen Sullivan

Conquer Cancer,® the ASCO Foundation, awarded $600,000 worth of grants to support studies addressing cancer care disparities in clinical trial enrollment for pediatric patients, and exploring new treatment options for prostate cancer that can reduce the chance of recurrence.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Conquer Cancer fuels five groundbreaking studies
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Conquer Cancer®, the ASCO Foundation, is accelerating discovery Institute-wide, from pediatrics to rare sarcomas.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Groundbreaking studies take aim at disparities and advanced disease
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Prostate Cancer Foundation (PCF) has awarded grants totaling more than $2.3 million to Dana-Farber researchers.

jetpack-related-posts.title: New grants advance key research across multiple disease areas
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Longtime Dana-Farber supporter Conquer Cancer,® the ASCO Foundation, recently awarded $1.45 million to support seven researchers pursuing projects in a wide range of disease areas.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Conquer Cancer® grants target several types of cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Conquer Cancer®, the ASCO Foundation, has fueled groundbreaking research at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute for decades.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Grants catalyze new advances in prostate cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Prostate Cancer Foundation has awarded $1.45 million in grants to three Dana-Farber investigators researching more powerful treatments for the disease.

jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Cookies for Kids’ Cancer has awarded two grants totaling $600,000 to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute to support groundbreaking pediatric cancer research.

Fall 2023
By Colleen Sullivan
Photography by Sam Ogden

Our historic partner, the Dana Foundation, made a new $100,000 commitment to the Defy Cancer Fund, which provides unrestricted support for The Dana-Farber Campaign. These flexible funds propel innovative early stage research, speed new drugs into clinical trials, retain and attract top talent; meet unanticipated needs; and ensure that we are fully serving our patients’ physical, emotional, psychological, and spiritual needs.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Campaign
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The success of our mission hinges on unrestricted gifts, including those raised through the Defy Cancer Fund.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Together in action, together in progress: Giving Day surpasses fundraising goal
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: This year’s annual Giving Day marked an especially generous occasion for dedicated supporters of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Unrestricted support: A powerful vote of confidence
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Dana-Farber Campaign is a catalyst for giving at every level, including through the Defy Cancer Fund, and has inspired tremendous unrestricted support from our generous philanthropic community.

img.alt_text: An image of a scientist looking through a test tube (image has blue overlay)

jetpack-related-posts.title: Giving Day celebrates 75 years of progress
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On May 22, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund held its fourth annual Giving Day—an inspirational day of hope, where supporters come together as a community to raise critical funds to defy cancer.

img.alt_text: A pediatric cancer patient smiling and holding a cookie

jetpack-related-posts.title: Arbella plays an MVP role in the Jimmy Fund’s mission to strike out cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A longtime partner of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund, Arbella Insurance Group continued its steadfast support of Dana-Farber’s mission throughout 2023, living out the company’s motto of: “Here. For Good.”

img.alt_text: A group of people holding an over-sized check at Fenway Park

jetpack-related-posts.title: Brenda McAdam
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: After being diagnosed with cholangiocarcinoma, a rare bile duct cancer, in August 2022, Brenda McAdam established the Brenda McAdam Fund for Bile Duct Cancer Research at Dana-Farber under the direction of James Cleary, MD, PhD. With her $100,000 gift, she hopes Cleary can help patients like her defy this rare…

Fall 2023
By Katherine Agate
Photography by Natasha Moustache Photography

The Friends of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute recently held their Annual Gala, raising more than $465,000. Evening with Friends featured cocktails, dinner, and a live auction. The Friends exemplify the “power of friends” through their dual mission: raising funds to support research, patient services, breast and gynecologic cancer programs, and oncology fellowships; and providing services that enhance Dana-Farber’s healing environment.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Friends of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Friends of Dana-Farber hosted a variety of events throughout 2024 that raised more than $600,000 for lifesaving cancer research and patient care.

jetpack-related-posts.title: PopStroke
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: PopStroke completed its second annual October Breast Cancer Awareness Initiative, last year, in partnership with Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund. Throughout October, PopStroke locations nationally ran a number of initiatives to support breast cancer research and patient care at Dana-Farber, raising close to $145,000.

jetpack-related-posts.title: An Evening with Friends
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On May 4, the Friends of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute gathered for a special evening that raised more than $400,000. Since 1976, the Friends have raised more than $50 million for Dana-Farber’s lifesaving mission.

img.alt_text: A group of people in front of a Friends of Dana-Farber sign

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Society
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Dana-Farber Society (DFS) is a group of visionary donors who are changing lives and creating a legacy through a planned gift such as a bequest, life income gift, or beneficiary designation to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, the Jimmy Fund, the Friends of Dana-Farber, or the Pan-Mass Challenge.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Palm Beach community rallies to surpass annual fundraising goal
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Palm Beach community once again demonstrated remarkable generosity by raising over $1.31 million to support Dana-Farber Cancer Institute through their Palm Beach Annual appeal.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Palm Beach surpasses $67 million in gifts to The Dana-Farber Campaign
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: For over three decades, the compassionate community in Palm Beach, Florida, has provided generous support for Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s lifesaving mission to conquer cancer in adults and children—not only in Boston and Palm Beach, but also across the country and around the world.

Fall 2023
By Colleen Sullivan

The Gastric Cancer Foundation gave $100,000 to support the research of Dana-Farber’s Nilay Sethi, MD, PhD, who is investigating treatments for gastric cancers with homologous recombination (HR) deficiencies that have proven effective in other types of HR-deficient cancers.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The DeGregorio Family Foundation continues to advance gastroesophageal cancer treatment
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Gastric and esophageal cancers often resist chemotherapy and metastasize easily. The DeGregorio Family Foundation aims to address this challenge with more than $500,000 in grant funding to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute to develop new treatments.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Irene Derocher
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Irene fulfilled Paul Derocher’s wishes by giving $100,000 to establish the Paul Derocher Fund for Small Intestine Cancer Research. Derocher’s support is enabling Dana-Farber’s Nilay Sethi, MD, PhD, to continue his research into better early detection and treatment strategies for small intestine cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Gabrielle’s Angel Foundation for Cancer Research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Gabrielle’s Angel Foundation for Cancer Research awarded $250,000 to Dana-Farber’s Zuzana Tothova, MD, PhD, who is exploring the biology of cohesin mutations, frequent and recurrent drivers of myelodysplastic syndromes and acute myeloid leukemia. With this funding, Tothova aims to develop targeted treatments for these cancers.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Sergio and Magda Brosio
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Sergio and Magda Brosio gave $100,000 to support the Center for Esophageal and Gastric Cancer’s biobank, with the hope that their gift inspires others. Motivated by their gratitude for Sergio’s physicians, Robert J. Mayer, MD, and Scott J. Swanson, MD, their philanthropy will expand tissue sample collection, which fuels clinical…

jetpack-related-posts.title: American Cancer Society grants propel research and programs forward
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The American Cancer Society (ACS) recently awarded more than $3.1 million in grants to 11 Dana-Farber Cancer Institute investigators. These grants support various areas across Dana-Farber, including research on improved outcomes and patient assistance programming to help with access to care.

jetpack-related-posts.title: American Gastroenterological Association Research Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The American Gastroenterological Association Research Foundation's generous grant of $100,000 supports the research of Dana-Farber’s Harshabad (Harsh) Singh, MBBS. This funding empowers him to further explore the biological foundations of HER2-driven gastric tumors and test innovative therapies. This can potentially transform treatment approaches for this challenging disease.

Fall 2023
By Colleen Sullivan

The Greenwall Foundation made a generous grant of more than $240,000 to support a Dana-Farber-led study into sustainability and conservation ethics in clinical decision-making, as part of the foundation’s mission to make bioethics an integral part of health care, policy, and research.

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Legacy of Leadership and Hope: The Elaine and Eduardo Saverin Foundation’s generational commitment to patients with metastatic breast cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Elaine and Eduardo Saverin Foundation has made an extraordinary $20 million grant to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute to accelerate research and care for people living with stage IV breast cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Lustgarten grant accelerates therapeutic discovery in pancreatic cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Lustgarten Foundation is the largest private funder of pancreatic cancer research in the world, funding preeminent pancreatic cancer researchers, driving the pursuit of bold and innovative science toward earlier detection and better treatments, and transforming pancreatic cancer into a curable disease.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Damon Runyon Cancer Research Foundation invests in tomorrow’s discoveries
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber received over $3,156,000 in grants from the Damon Runyon Cancer Research Foundation in 2024 supporting 10 physician-scientists and researchers.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Lymphoma Research Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: As part of their mission to fund innovative research at top institutions around the country, the Lymphoma Research Foundation’s recent funding cycle included awarding grants totaling $115,000 to fund two Dana-Farber studies into advanced treatment options for patients diagnosed with T-cell lymphoma and mantle cell lymphoma.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The National Breast Cancer Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The National Breast Cancer Foundation has made a generous gift of $170,000 to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute as part of their ongoing support. This latest gift plays a crucial role in advancing our mission to defy cancer and enhance breast cancer patient outcomes.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Ambrose Monell Foundation fuels critical immunotherapy priorities
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: By encouraging strategic risk-taking and rewarding experimentation and new ideas, the Ambrose Monell Foundation is empowering Dana-Farber to capitalize on its collective expertise to develop a new generation of innovative cancer-fighting immunotherapies tailored to the specific needs of patients.

Fall 2023
By Colleen Sullivan

With a $224,000 grant, Innovation in Cancer Informatics is funding a project at Dana-Farber that will develop and pilot a new mobile health application that integrates patients’ electronic health records to better support them, and their care teams, in management of advanced cancer pain.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Innovation in Cancer Informatics
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Innovation in Cancer Informatics awarded $224,000 to support investigations led by Sylvan Baca, MD, PhD, and Eliezer Van Allen, MD, into circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA). This research will analyze tumor features and aims to, for the first time, guide therapy selection in breast cancer with low levels of ctDNA.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Ambrose Monell Foundation fuels critical immunotherapy priorities
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: By encouraging strategic risk-taking and rewarding experimentation and new ideas, the Ambrose Monell Foundation is empowering Dana-Farber to capitalize on its collective expertise to develop a new generation of innovative cancer-fighting immunotherapies tailored to the specific needs of patients.

jetpack-related-posts.title: American Cancer Society grants propel research and programs forward
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The American Cancer Society (ACS) recently awarded more than $3.1 million in grants to 11 Dana-Farber Cancer Institute investigators. These grants support various areas across Dana-Farber, including research on improved outcomes and patient assistance programming to help with access to care.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Prostate Cancer Foundation fuels Dana-Farber innovation with $1M+ in grants
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: PCF recently awarded $1,050,000 to three Dana-Farber Cancer Institute researchers through two Young Investigator Awards and one Challenge Award, each supporting research projects aimed at combating prostate cancer and improving outcomes for patients.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Eliminating disparities to improve outcomes
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With philanthropic support from the Scarlet Feather Fund, Dana-Farber’s Kira Bona, MD, MPH, and Christopher Lathan, MD, MS, MPH, chief clinical access and equity officer and the Hadley Family Chair at Dana-Farber, are leading bold, innovative approaches that aim to reduce disparities in outcomes for adult and pediatric cancer patients.

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Legacy of Leadership and Hope: The Elaine and Eduardo Saverin Foundation’s generational commitment to patients with metastatic breast cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Elaine and Eduardo Saverin Foundation has made an extraordinary $20 million grant to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute to accelerate research and care for people living with stage IV breast cancer.

Fall 2023
By Shannon Watterson
Photography by John Deputy

In June, adult and pediatric patients and their families joined donors and sponsors for a once-in-a-lifetime chance to step up to the plate at Fenway Park. Jimmy Fund Day at Fenway presented by DraftKings raised $223,000 thanks to stand-out fundraisers like Team Russo and many others giving generously to strike out cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jimmy Fund Day at Fenway
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In September 2025, dreams became reality as more than 200 participants, including Dana-Farber patients, had the once-in-a lifetime chance to play ball at Fenway Park. Thanks to generous support from sponsors, the Boston Red Sox, fundraising teams, and donors, Jimmy Fund Day at Fenway presented by DraftKings raised more than…

img.alt_text: Three people at Fenway Park wearing Jimmy Fund jerseys

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon breaks records with $5.7 million raised for Dana-Farber
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The WEEI/NESN Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon presented by Arbella Insurance continued to be a beacon of support for Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund in August with a record-breaking fundraising year.

img.alt_text: Ali Kelleher cheering at Fenway Park

jetpack-related-posts.title: Pan-Mass Challenge celebrates PMC Pedal Partners from the Jimmy Fund Clinic at Fenway Park
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On May 17, dozens of PMC Pedal Partners—pediatric patients from the Jimmy Fund Clinic at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute paired with PMC riders and teams—gathered at The 521 Overlook at Fenway Park to meet the cyclists participating in the 46th PMC on Aug. 2 and 3.

img.alt_text: A family of four at Fenway Park

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jimmy Fund Day at Fenway
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Jimmy Fund Day at Fenway presented by DraftKings raised $230,000 to support innovative cancer research and compassionate patient care at Dana-Farber. Thanks to donor support, Dana-Farber patients and their families were able to participate in this unforgettable experience and take the field at Fenway Park.

img.alt_text: Jimmy Fund Day at Fenway logo

jetpack-related-posts.title: Another home run year for the Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The WEEI/NESN Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon presented by Arbella Insurance helped strike out cancer for the 22nd year at Fenway Park in August, raising nearly $4 million for adult and pediatric cancer care and research at Dana-Farber.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Milestone 20th annual WEEI/NESN Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon raises $3.5 million
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Since 1953, the Boston Red Sox have had a deep and multifaceted impact on patients with cancer through its strong partnership with Dana-Farber and the Jimmy Fund.

img.alt_text: Dana-Farber patient and doctor on the field at Fenway Park

Fall 2023
By Colleen Sullivan

Jay and Kristy Ladieu gave $125,000 to support melanoma research under the direction of Megan Insco, MD, PhD, at Dana-Farber. Fueled by this gift, Insco and her team are pursuing studies into the biology of melanoma, laying the groundwork for critically needed treatment options.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Melanoma Research Alliance
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Since its founding in 2007, the Melanoma Research Alliance has become the largest nonprofit funder of crucial melanoma research worldwide. In 2025, they awarded $430,000 in grants to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute supporting the work of Rizwan Haq, MD, PhD, Giacomo Oliveira, PhD, and David Liu, MD, MPH, MS, to advance…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Karen O’Connor and Bruce MacGregor
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Karen O’Connor and Bruce MacGregor renewed their support for the O’Connor-MacGregor Fund for Melanoma Research with a new $150,000 commitment. This latest gift will support research into the underlying drivers of melanoma and development of durable therapeutic options under the direction of Rizwan Haq, MD, PhD.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Brian and Jane Crowley
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Brian and Jane Crowley gave $100,000 to support the work of F. Stephan Hodi Jr., MD, director of the Melanoma Center and the Sharon Crowley Martin Chair in Melanoma at Dana-Farber. Bolstered by this generous funding, Hodi is pursuing innovative research into new therapeutic approaches for melanoma.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Kittredges continue generous support of melanoma and immuno-oncology research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Francis Kittredge, MD, JD, and his wife, Adele, know that supporting Dana-Farber Cancer Institute makes a difference because their philanthropy already has—and their impact continues to grow through their ongoing generosity.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Georgette and John Heerwagen
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Georgette and John Heerwagen recently renewed their support for lung cancer research at Dana-Farber with a generous gift of $125,000. Under the direction of David Jackman, MD, in collaboration with David Barbie, MD, both faculty in the Lowe Center for Thoracic Oncology at Dana-Farber, this funding will enable researchers to…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Melanoma Research Alliance advances personalized immunotherapies
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A $900,000 Team Science grant will advance collaboration and innovation in immunotherapies for melanoma at Dana-Farber.

content.rendered:
Fall 2023
By Katherine Agate

Martha Massey increased a recent pledge by $100,000 to support the research of Robert Soiffer, MD, the Worthington and Margaret Collette Professor of Medicine. In memory of her beloved husband, Calvin, Massey’s expanded support enables Soiffer to further research in the drug venetoclax for hematologic malignancies.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Kesslers’ vision for advancing AML research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Kesslers donated $1 million to advance AML research led by Robert Soiffer, MD, chief of the Division of Hematologic Malignancies and Worthington and Margaret Collette Professor of Medicine in the Field of Hematologic Oncology at Harvard Medical School. This substantial gift will empower Soiffer and his team to continue…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dienna and John Lehner
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dienna and John Lehner recommended a gift totaling $100,000 to the board of the Orchard Foundation, to support leukemia research under the direction of Dana-Farber researchers, Robert Soiffer, MD, and Daniel DeAngelo, MD, PhD.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Leukemia & Lymphoma Society attacks rare and resistant blood cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Leukemia & Lymphoma Society (LLS) has awarded six grants totaling $5.8 million to Dana-Farber investigators.

img.alt_text: An artist’s rendering of bone marrow cells showing acute myeloid leukemia.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Robert and Margaret King
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Robert and Margaret King made a gift of $100,000, supporting melanoma research under the direction of Megan Insco, MD, PhD. Their generous donation advances critical studies in the development of novel therapeutic approaches for the most difficult-to-treat melanomas, while enhancing clinical care for patients affected by this challenging disease.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Crowley gift accelerates innovative research in chronic lymphocytic leukemia
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Brian and Jane Crowley are longtime supporters of Dana-Farber who made their first gift nearly two decades ago to advance melanoma research in memory of Brian’s sister.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Michael and Margaret Kerr
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Michael and Margaret Kerr established the Kerr Family Fund for Translational Research at Dana-Farber with a $100,000 gift in 2023. The fund will be directed by James Cleary, MD, PhD, whom the couple laud for his compassionate patient care.

content.rendered:
Fall 2023
By Colleen Sullivan

Ovarian cancer is often difficult to treat at later stages and difficult to detect at earlier stages. With a $100,000 grant, the Minnesota Ovarian Cancer Alliance is supporting research at Dana-Farber into the development of an ultrasensitive blood test to detect ovarian cancer at its earliest, and most treatable, stages.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Kicks for Cancer harnesses power of community to drive cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Nearly 20 years ago, Concord-Carlisle High School hosted its first Kicks for Cancer soccer match to honor the memory of Lois Wells, the mother of assistant men’s soccer coach Steve Wells, who passed away from ovarian cancer. Today, Kicks for Cancer has grown into a vibrant week-long celebration that unites…

img.alt_text: Soccer players mid-game on the field

jetpack-related-posts.title: Gift to ovarian cancer inspired by story of research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In early 2022, Dr. Jean Kasmer read a story in Impact about an ovarian cancer survivor who gave to support the research of Ursula Matulonis, MD, chief of the division of Gynecologic Oncology and the Brock-Wilson Family Chair at Dana-Farber.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Tina’s Wish
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Longtime supporter Tina’s Wish recently awarded more than $450,000 over a two-year period to support two Dana-Farber studies into early detection for ovarian cancer—one investigating a new class of microRNA and key biomarkers and how they could be used to develop a personalized blood test, and another examining how epigenetic…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Johnston gift paves the way for a novel ovarian cancer clinical trial
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Debbie Johnston is dedicated to supporting causes that are close to her heart, and Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s ovarian cancer research is one such cause.

jetpack-related-posts.title: DeFeo gift aims to push ovarian cancer treatment to next level
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The late Dara Frigoletto DeFeo was a giver, her husband, Peter DeFeo, recalls fondly. Whether it was reading to small children in Dana-Farber’s Jimmy Fund Clinic or helping a senior citizen pluck an item off a high shelf at the grocery store, Dara “had a unique way to communicate that…

img.alt_text: A close-up photo of Dara Frigoletto DeFeo

jetpack-related-posts.title: girlygirl P.A.R.T.S. surpasses $1 million
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The girlygirl P.A.R.T.S. 5K/Walk for Ovarian Cancer has surpassed $1 million in total funds raised since 2009, supporting research at Dana-Farber.

Fall 2023
By Colleen Sullivan
Photography by Bryce Vickmark

The Mugar Foundation made a generous commitment of $500,000 to support the previously established Mugar Family Fellowship in Lung Cancer. While advancing promising lung cancer research, the fellowship provides reliable funding for an early career scientist to pursue innovative research and develop the skills needed to lead the future of lung cancer research.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Schaubert Family endows visionary fellowship for lung cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: For nearly a decade, the Schaubert family has been a dedicated supporter of lung cancer research at Dana-Farber.

img.alt_text: Eileen Schaubert (center) and her daughters, Suzanne and Amy.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Polly and Ming Tsai
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Polly and Ming Tsai made a generous new commitment to advance research by David Barbie, MD, and the Lowe Center for Thoracic Oncology designed to increase the durability, precision, and effectiveness of lung cancer treatments, like the promising CAR T-cell therapy already in development with previous support from the Tsais.

img.alt_text: Chef Ming Tsai and his wife Polly pose for a photo outside in winter

jetpack-related-posts.title: National Cancer Center
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: National Cancer Center awarded fellowship grants to Dana-Farber totaling $328,000. One new grant will support Katharina Hoebel, MD, PhD, in developing personalized treatment for non-small cell lung cancer through the use of artificial intelligence. With a second new commitment, Diego Martinez Alonso, PhD, will explore how to utilize CDK4/6 inhibitors…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Georgette and John Heerwagen
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Georgette and John Heerwagen recently renewed their support for lung cancer research at Dana-Farber with a generous gift of $125,000. Under the direction of David Jackman, MD, in collaboration with David Barbie, MD, both faculty in the Lowe Center for Thoracic Oncology at Dana-Farber, this funding will enable researchers to…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Clifford Family
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Clifford Family established the Woolley-Clifford Foundation Fund with a $100,000 gift, supporting the research of David Kozono, MD, PhD, as he works to investigate blood and tissue-based biomarkers in lung cancer patients that can help predict lung inflammation and anti-tumor response following radiation therapy.

img.alt_text: Liquid pouring from a beaker into a petri dish

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Norman J. Fisher & Doris Fisher Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Norman J. Fisher & Doris Fisher Foundation recently renewed their support for the Michael C. Gohl Fellowship with a generous $350,000 gift. This fellowship in thoracic oncology supports a promising early career scientist working in the lab of Pasi Jänne, MD, PhD.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Campaign: Closing the equity gap in cancer care
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Funds from The Dana-Farber Campaign allow us to expand access to underserved populations and improve research to reduce disparities in treatment outcomes.

img.alt_text: Patient Navigator Judy Thyme, MSPH (left), assists patient Carle Price with her medications.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Groundbreaking studies take aim at disparities and advanced disease
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Prostate Cancer Foundation (PCF) has awarded grants totaling more than $2.3 million to Dana-Farber researchers.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Prostate Cancer Foundation fuels Dana-Farber innovation with $1M+ in grants
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: PCF recently awarded $1,050,000 to three Dana-Farber Cancer Institute researchers through two Young Investigator Awards and one Challenge Award, each supporting research projects aimed at combating prostate cancer and improving outcomes for patients.

jetpack-related-posts.title: National Foundation for Cancer Research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber recently received a $110,000 grant from the National Foundation for Cancer Research to study new, non-invasive approaches to identify specific subtypes of kidney cancer and particular genetic alterations in prostate cancer, with the aim of creating earlier detection and treatment interventions for patients with these diseases.

img.alt_text: National Foundation for Cancer Research logo

jetpack-related-posts.title: First-ever fellowship in metastatic prostate cancer and AI research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Tom and Olivia McDonough's gift fuels collaboration to harness the power of AI and speed development of novel therapies against prostate cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Grants catalyze new advances in prostate cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Prostate Cancer Foundation has awarded $1.45 million in grants to three Dana-Farber investigators researching more powerful treatments for the disease.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dana-Farber Cancer Institute Presidential Symposium
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In October, Dana-Farber supporters and leaders gathered for the annual Dana-Farber Cancer Institute Presidential Symposium. Attendees received firsthand updates on the State of the Institute, advances and opportunities in prevention and early detection, the impact of philanthropy on advancing research, and Dana-Farber’s world-renowned hematology/oncology fellowship program. Pictured are fellowship program…

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Hale Family receives the Sidney Farber Medical Research Award
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In November 2023, Dana-Farber Trustee Judy Hale, Dana-Farber Trustee Karen Hale, Rob Hale, Elizabeth Hale Kendall, and Richard Kendall were awarded the Sidney Farber Medical Research Award in recognition of the Hale Family’s outstanding contributions and service to the Institute for many decades.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Leukemia & Lymphoma Society grants target blood cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Leukemia & Lymphoma Society recently awarded more than $7.3 million in grants to Dana-Farber researchers in its quest to better understand and find cures for blood cancers.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Whittaker Family Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Stephani Batchelor and Andrew Robert Whittaker made an additional gift of $225,000 to Dana-Farber’s Lynch Syndrome Center. This gift supports the leadership of Sapna Syngal, MD, MPH, and Matthew Yurgelun, MD, FASCO, CGAF, and their team in diagnosing Lynch syndrome and advancing screenings, treatments, and prevention strategies to help patients…

img.alt_text: Various tubes and other lab equipment

jetpack-related-posts.title: Breast Cancer Research Foundation continues support with nearly $4 million in grants
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Since its founding by the late Evelyn Lauder alongside her dear friend Larry Norton, MD, in 1993, the Breast Cancer Research Foundation (BCRF) has championed research as the key to one day curing breast cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Eliminating disparities to improve outcomes
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With philanthropic support from the Scarlet Feather Fund, Dana-Farber’s Kira Bona, MD, MPH, and Christopher Lathan, MD, MS, MPH, chief clinical access and equity officer and the Hadley Family Chair at Dana-Farber, are leading bold, innovative approaches that aim to reduce disparities in outcomes for adult and pediatric cancer patients.

content.rendered:
Fall 2023
By Katherine Agate
Photography by Michael Blanchard

In memory of their dear friend, Melanie Rosay, Jeff Silveira and Beth Logan recently made a $250,000 gift toward the Melanie Rosay Fund for Breast Cancer Research at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. The fund, established in 2020 through gifts from friends and family of Melanie, seeks to raise $1 million to provide support for metastatic breast cancer research under Dana-Farber’s Rinath Jeselsohn, MD.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Donor bequeaths $1 million gift to metastatic breast cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Through an estate provision added to her will, Anne P. Olsen has bequeathed $1 million to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. The gift will be directed to the Hilary J. Olsen Fund for Metastatic Breast Cancer, which was established in 2019 by Anne’s son, Jeff. The fund is in memory of Jeff’s…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Carney family remains steadfast in support of breast cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With a recent $1 million gift, the Carney Family Charitable Foundation, led by Trustees Patrick and Lillian Carney, has expanded a legacy of support for breast cancer immuno-oncology research at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute that spans over 20 years.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Freedlander bequest focuses on inflammatory breast cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The estate of Ruth Freedlander made a $1.8 million bequest to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute that will advance research into inflammatory breast cancer (IBC), a rare and aggressive disease that is particularly difficult to treat.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Michael Swidler
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber Cancer Institute received a gracious contribution from Michael Swidler to establish the Nancy Swidler Fund for Breast Cancer Research in honor of his late wife. Managed by Sara Tolaney, MD, MPH, this fund is intended to advance pioneering breast cancer research and create pathways to better outcomes for every…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Eisenson encourages CGAs as a simple and lasting legacy
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Supporting cancer research and care at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute can take many forms that benefit both the Institute and the donor. Michael Eisenson (pictured), Institute Trustee and chair of The Dana-Farber Campaign, recently established a charitable gift annuity (CGA) with a generous gift of $250,000.

img.alt_text: Michael Eisenson at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute's healing garden

jetpack-related-posts.title: PopStroke
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: PopStroke completed its second annual October Breast Cancer Awareness Initiative, last year, in partnership with Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund. Throughout October, PopStroke locations nationally ran a number of initiatives to support breast cancer research and patient care at Dana-Farber, raising close to $145,000.

title.rendered: Strike Out Cancer with the Jimmy Fund

content.rendered:
Fall 2023
By Shannon Watterson

As the Red Sox returned to Fenway Park this spring, the Jimmy Fund community came together to cheer them on and support Dana-Farber patients. Rally Against CancerSM teams celebrated Opening Day on March 30 and more than 100 fans signed up to strike out cancer by donating for every Red Sox win, raising $240,000 in total. Go, Sox!
