title.rendered: Giving Day celebrates 75 years of progress

content.rendered:
Fall 2023
By Casey Reis

On May 22, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund held its fourth annual Giving Day—an inspirational day of hope, where supporters come together as a community to raise critical funds to defy cancer. This year’s Giving Day was particularly notable, as it fell on the 75th anniversary of the radio broadcast that launched the Jimmy Fund. Supporters helped celebrate 75 years of research, discovery, and extraordinary patient care by raising over $622,000 from more than 6,200 gifts, surpassing the fundraising goal of $500,000. This success was due in part to an anonymous Dana-Farber Trustee who generously matched $250,000 of gifts to The Dana-Farber Campaign’s Defy Cancer Fund.

In the weeks leading up to Giving Day, the family of pediatric patient, Eva, shared their story with the Jimmy Fund community, encouraging supporters across the country to join Dana-Farber in its lifesaving mission. Three years ago, Eva was diagnosed with B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia and has since undergone numerous surgeries, rounds of chemotherapy, and a stem cell transplant from her twin brother. Today, thanks to cutting-edge treatment at Dana-Farber, Eva is a happy and healthy 5-year-old, with no evidence of leukemic cells. 

“If it weren’t for Dana-Farber, we wouldn’t be where we are now, as a family, planning for Eva’s future,” says Laurie, Eva’s mother. “Defying cancer means finding a way. Leukemia is crafty. It’s sneaky. It hides. Our team always had a new avenue to take, a new treatment to try, and a belief that we are stronger than leukemia.”

While navigating the uncertainties surrounding her daughter’s cancer diagnosis has been difficult, Laurie is grateful to have the support of an extended network of people who love and care for Eva and her family—some of whom they’ve never met,  like Giving Day donors.

As the Jimmy Fund celebrates 75 years of groundbreaking scientific discovery and lifesaving treatment, the generosity of the Giving Day community will help fuel innovation and progress so more patients like Eva can look toward a cancer-free future. The majority of the funds raised on Giving Day were directed to the Defy Cancer Fund—unrestricted funding that propels innovative early stage research; accelerates clinical trials; allows Dana-Farber to attract and retain the best researchers, clinicians, and staff; and ensures all patients have access to programs that address their physical, emotional, psychological, and spiritual needs.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Together in action, together in progress: Giving Day surpasses fundraising goal
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: This year’s annual Giving Day marked an especially generous occasion for dedicated supporters of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Inspiring hope: Catherine’s journey and the impact of Giving Day
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund’s annual Giving Day, held on Wednesday, May 21 this year, united patients, families, employees, and supporters worldwide in giving to Dana-Farber's mission to defy cancer.

img.alt_text: A woman sitting in a hospital bed with her two young children

jetpack-related-posts.title: Boston Marathon® Jimmy Fund Walk celebrates 35 years of inspiration and impact
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Last fall, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute patients, families, and supporters joined forces to defy cancer at the 35th annual Boston Marathon® Jimmy Fund Walk presented by Hyundai, which raises the most money of any single-day walk in the nation.

img.alt_text: A group of Jimmy Fund Walk participants pose for a photo in their Walk t-shirts

jetpack-related-posts.title: GivingTuesday inspires thousands to defy cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: For many, Thanksgiving weekend marks the start of the holiday season, with family gatherings and a spirit of gratitude in the air. Since 2012, GivingTuesday celebrates this special time of year by encouraging charitable giving on the Tuesday after Black Friday and Cyber Monday shopping.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Back on course with the Boston Marathon® Jimmy Fund Walk
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: For 34 years, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute supporters have come together for a day of inspiration and hope at the Boston Marathon® Jimmy Fund Walk presented by Hyundai, raising lifesaving funds to defy cancer for patients everywhere.

img.alt_text: Walkers and volunteers on the route of the Boston Marathon Jimmy Fund Walk

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Campaign
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: One way our supporters accelerate campaign efforts is by including Dana-Farber in their estate plans.

title.rendered: Jimmy Fund Day kicks off 75th Anniversary

content.rendered:
Fall 2023
By Lori Dougherty
Photography by Kamissa Barry, John Deputy, Theresa Johnson Herlihy, Sam Ogden

The Jimmy Fund launched its 75th anniversary year on May 22 with a day of events highlighting its rich history and lasting impact. Proclaimed Jimmy Fund Day by Boston Mayor Michelle Wu, the day began with a ceremony at the Yawkey Center for Cancer Care. Dana-Farber patients and families joined President and CEO Laurie H. Glimcher, MD, to unveil commemorative signage and a life-sized cow sculpture, both decorated with the Jimmy Fund’s “We’re All Jimmy” slogan in multiple languages. The cow sculpture was part of CowParade New England presented by Herb Chambers, an art installation that ran from June through early September throughout Boston, with proceeds benefitting The Dana-Farber Campaign.

Mid-day, a special gathering in Chestnut Hill honored members of families, organizations, and Official Charity Partners whose efforts helped launch the Jimmy Fund in 1948 and continue to sustain its growth.

“The Jimmy Fund has enabled Dana-Farber to become one of the world’s leading centers of cancer research and treatment, saving countless lives.”

— President & CEO Laurie H. Glimcher, MD

The celebration continued at dusk, when iconic Boston-area landmarks participated in “Light Boston Blue for the Jimmy Fund,” illuminating in the Jimmy Fund’s signature color, and area billboards carried commemorative Jimmy Fund messages into the evening. Recognition of the anniversary is continuing throughout the year, at various Jimmy Fund events.

“As we mark the Jimmy Fund’s 75-year anniversary, we take pride in remaining anchored by the core principles of Dr. Sidney Farber’s mission: to make scientific discoveries and turn them into lifesaving treatments,” President Glimcher said. “The Jimmy Fund has enabled Dana-Farber to become one of the world’s leading centers of cancer research and treatment, saving countless lives.”

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jimmy Fund Golf community helps to usher in the Jimmy Fund’s 75th
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Jimmy Fund Golf presented by Mohegan Sun marked another ace year in 2023, with an array of dedicated tournament directors, sponsors, and supporters across the country raising more than $6.8 million for The Dana-Farber Campaign.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Red Sox name 2023 Jimmy Fund Captain
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Boston Red Sox pitcher, Garrett Whitlock, has been named Jimmy Fund Captain for the 2023 baseball season.

img.alt_text: Jimmy Fund Captain Garrett Whitlock in the Fenway dugout with pediatric patient Lily

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Message from Melany Duval
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: When Dr. Sidney Farber achieved the first remissions in childhood leukemia in 1947, he changed everything.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Boston Marathon® Jimmy Fund Walk celebrates 35 years of inspiration and impact
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Last fall, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute patients, families, and supporters joined forces to defy cancer at the 35th annual Boston Marathon® Jimmy Fund Walk presented by Hyundai, which raises the most money of any single-day walk in the nation.

img.alt_text: A group of Jimmy Fund Walk participants pose for a photo in their Walk t-shirts

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Herb Chambers Companies surpasses $1 million in gifts
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Herb Chambers Companies, one of New England’s largest auto dealers, has been a powerful ally and supporter of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund since 2015.

img.alt_text: Herb Chambers and his partner, Melissa Lees, with the cow she created, Chin Up, during the CowParade New England Preview Party.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Giving Day celebrates 75 years of progress
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On May 22, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund held its fourth annual Giving Day—an inspirational day of hope, where supporters come together as a community to raise critical funds to defy cancer.

img.alt_text: A pediatric cancer patient smiling and holding a cookie

title.rendered: The Jimmy Fund: 75 years of impact

content.rendered:
Fall 2023
By Lori Dougherty
Photography by Getty Images, Sam Ogden

Since the seminal radio broadcast in 1948 that introduced the nation to a young cancer patient dubbed “Jimmy” and the researchers and clinicians dedicated to caring for children with cancer, the Jimmy Fund’s generous community of supporters has contributed an incredible total of more than $1.5 billion so far, to help Dana-Farber Cancer Institute defy cancer for adults and children everywhere.

Gifts large and small, from across the country and around the world, continue to fuel groundbreaking advances in research and patient care for all forms of cancer—even the rarest and most difficult to treat. While there is much more work to be done, here is just a small sampling of the progress made possible by gifts to the Jimmy Fund.

1952
Dr. Sidney Farber hires the nation’s first full-time oncology social worker, enhancing his concept of Total Patient Care.

1954
Dana-Farber researchers achieve the first remissions in Wilms tumor of the kidney, a common childhood cancer, boosting cure rates from 40 to 85%.

1958
The Jimmy Fund Building adds four floors, furthering Dr. Farber’s revolutionary vision of research labs and patient clinics under one roof. The building was originally completed in 1952 with help from Jimmy Fund supporters.

1963
Dana-Farber researchers develop the means to collect and transfuse blood-clotting factors called platelets, to combat bleeding—a common side effect of chemotherapy.

1973
Dana-Farber launches the first clinical trials for children diagnosed with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL), laying the foundation for today’s cure rates of 85 to 90%.

1988
Two out of every three children who enter the Jimmy Fund Clinic are cured.

1993
Dana-Farber establishes the High Risk Research Clinic, one of the nation’s first genetic testing programs for members of families with an inherited susceptibility to cancer.

1998
The Institute establishes the first Adult Patient and Family Advisory Council in the U.S., now a national model for patient-centered care.

2001
Dana-Farber basic scientists discover how a protein called PD-L1 helps cancer cells evade attack by the immune system, leading to FDA approval of a new class of immunotherapy drugs.

2012
Dana-Farber establishes the Cancer Care Equity Program to reduce disparities in cancer outcomes and create a national model for translating research into interventions.

2019
In response to the alarming rise of colorectal cancer in people under age 50, Dana-Farber opens the Young-Onset Colorectal Cancer Center, one of the first of its kind.

2021
Following a clinical trial led by Dana-Farber, the FDA grants its first approval for CAR T-cell therapy for adults with multiple myeloma.

2023
The FDA grants accelerated approval for a novel metastatic breast cancer (MBC) treatment based on an international clinical trial co-led by Dana-Farber.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Jimmy Fund celebrates 75 years
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On May 22, 1948, Einar Gustafson, a young boy being treated for lymphoma by Dr. Sidney Farber and dubbed “Jimmy” to protect his privacy, shared his story from his hospital bed.

img.alt_text: The original Jimmy in a hospital bed with an old TV

jetpack-related-posts.title: Chairmen of the Jimmy Fund: building community since 1948
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Since the earliest days of the Jimmy Fund, passionate and committed individuals have devoted their time, talents, resources, and relationships to raising money in support of a powerful possibility: curing cancer for everyone.

img.alt_text: Larry Lucchino at the Boston Marathon Jimmy Fund Walk

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon breaks records with $5.7 million raised for Dana-Farber
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The WEEI/NESN Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon presented by Arbella Insurance continued to be a beacon of support for Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund in August with a record-breaking fundraising year.

img.alt_text: Ali Kelleher cheering at Fenway Park

jetpack-related-posts.title: Giving Day celebrates 75 years of progress
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On May 22, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund held its fourth annual Giving Day—an inspirational day of hope, where supporters come together as a community to raise critical funds to defy cancer.

img.alt_text: A pediatric cancer patient smiling and holding a cookie

jetpack-related-posts.title: Meet the new Co-Chairs of the Jimmy Fund: Brock Holt and Tom Caron
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Holt and Caron will be the lead ambassadors and public spokespeople on behalf of the Jimmy Fund, helping to raise funds and awareness.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Your generosity soars past $2 million on GivingTuesday
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On GivingTuesday 2024, Dana-Farber and the Jimmy Fund’s community of support far surpassed our $1 million goal.

content.rendered:
Fall 2023
By Colleen Sullivan

The first step in creating cutting-edge cancer treatments for patients is basic research—scientific investigation that uncovers biology’s fundamental principles and helps us understand how the cells and molecules in our bodies work. Such research, also known as “discovery science,” is a key strategic priority of The Dana-Farber Campaign because it fosters innovative studies that yield new clues about cancer—clues that can open entirely new avenues for exploration and may ultimately lead to revolutionary new treatments. For example:

Rizwan Haq, MD, PhD, and his colleagues have developed nine melanoma models, derived by gene editing melanocytes (precursors to melanoma) in order to study the biological pathways that drive melanoma metastasis. Haq’s studies, which explore the dependencies of metastasis, could lead to new therapeutic strategies to prevent the metastatic spread of melanoma.

Sarah Johnstone, MD, PhD, is investigating the mechanism by which two proteins, CTCF and BORIS, which are often mutated in ovarian cancers, reshape genome structure to facilitate tumor-promoting gene activity. Johnstone’s research aims to uncover vulnerabilities in tumor cells harboring these protein mutations, in order to identify therapeutic pathways that can be targeted in intractable ovarian cancers.

Shangming Tang, PhD, is studying a catastrophic mutational event called chromothripsis that occurs in about 30% of human cancers and can lead to drug resistance and relapse. Tang is investigating the role of the MPG pathway in chromothripsis and how it functions in normal cells to protect against genome instability. Learning more about how this process occurs could lay the groundwork for new cancer therapies.

The Claudia Adams Barr Program in Innovative Basic Cancer Research was founded by Institute Trustees Delores Barr Weaver and J. Wayne Weaver in honor of Delores’ mother, solely to advance basic, discovery science at Dana-Farber. One hundred percent of the funds raised by the dedicated runners of the Dana-Farber Marathon Challenge have provided more than $122 million in vital support for the program since 1990.

jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Many of today’s important advances in cancer care trace their origins to basic research—a form of scientific investigation aimed at uncovering the fundamental principles of biology, chemistry, and foundational science.

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Message from Melany Duval
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Science has long been the catalyst for transformative cancer care. More recently, we’ve witnessed revolutionary advances that have benefited patients and those who hold them dear.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Basic research is focus of Mathers Charitable Foundation grants
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The G. Harold and Leila Y. Mathers Charitable Foundation has awarded Dana-Farber $1.47 million to support two Institute researchers investigating how cancer develops and how cells detect and respond to viral infections.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Radical collaborations target intractable cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: BTC has awarded $22.9 million in grants to Dana-Farber researchers working across multiple institutions to unlock the secrets of four difficult-to-treat cancers and intercept or develop cutting-edge treatments for them.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Harrington Discovery Institute
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With a generous $460,000 contribution, the Harrington Discovery Institute is propelling innovative cancer research led by Min-Ru Wu, MD, PhD, and Loren Walensky, MD, PhD, as they work to develop less toxic treatments for melanoma patients and investigate targeted therapies for other drug-resistant cancers, respectively.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Russ Agrusa honors late wife by fueling colorectal cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Russ and his late wife, Paula, established the Project P Fund in 2014 with a goal of empowering researchers at Dana-Farber to develop more effective targeted and immune-based therapies for patients with colorectal cancer. content.rendered:
Summer 2023

Dear Friends,

It all started in 1948 with a 12-year-old boy with cancer dubbed “Jimmy,” who inspired thousands to give money in support of cancer research. Those first generous gifts sparked the Jimmy Fund, the charitable arm of Dana-Farber that has been going strong for 75 years, with support from an extraordinary community.

This year, more than ever, I have been reflecting on what an amazing time we are living in for cancer care. Treatments that we have today would have seemed impossible in 1948. And with so much more to do, just imagine the heights we will reach 75 years from now.

I imagine a world in which we have targeted treatments for every type of cancer in adults and children, new methods to routinely detect cancer early and prevent disease before it starts, advanced immunotherapies with minimal toxicities that are effective for all patients—I truly believe that all of this, and more, is possible.

Philanthropy enables progress—Dana-Farber and the Jimmy Fund are indelible proof of this. The Jimmy Fund’s legacy will forever be of a community coming together to ensure a better future for cancer patients. Whatever that future holds, it will be built by philanthropy, just as it was in 1948 when the world was first inspired by Jimmy. Thanks to the combined power of science and philanthropic compassion, Dana-Farber will continue to defy cancer for patients everywhere.

Thank you for your part in our history, and the continued part you will play in our future.

With gratitude,

Melany N. Duval
Senior Vice President and Chief Philanthropy Officer

content.rendered:
Summer 2023
By Brittany Flaherty

The Dana-Farber Campaign is an ambitious, multi-year fundraising effort to change the future of cancer research and care—the largest in the Institute’s history and one of the largest ever in the U.S. focused solely on cancer. Our community of support is crucial to this effort.

Developing next-generation cancer drugs is a top priority of The Dana-Farber Campaign. Dana-Farber is a global leader in drug discovery, playing a critical role in the development of more than half of all cancer drugs approved by the FDA in the past 5 years. Yet many cancer-causing proteins are not susceptible to drugs designed in the usual way and have been labeled as “undruggable”—a characterization we simply do not accept. With campaign support, we will engineer completely new classes of medicines that block cancer-promoting proteins in novel ways, delivering more next-generation drugs for adults and children with rare, difficult-to-treat, or recurrent cancers.

Gifts to advance drug development empower us to continue our leading-edge discovery, take risks, and uncover solutions. Together, we can Defy Cancer and develop next-generation cancer drugs for patients everywhere.

To learn more, visit DefyCancer.org.

excerpt.rendered: Dana-Farber has played a critical role in the development of more than half of all cancer drugs approved by the FDA in the past 5 years.

content.rendered:
Summer 2023
By Kayla Stravin
Photography by Aaron Washington

In 2022, Andrea McGrath celebrated 20 years since her successful stem cell transplant at Dana-Farber. She hosted a survivorship event, raising over $16,000 to benefit the work of her doctor and now friend, Corey Cutler, MD, MPH, FRCPC, whose advances in stem cell transplantation are continuing to improve outcomes for blood disorder patients like her.

jetpack-related-posts.title: John and Hallie Dovich Fund
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Hallie and John Dovich generously gifted $100,000 to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, establishing the John and Hallie Dovich Fund. Under the direction of Vincent Ho, MD, this fund will support stem cell transplantation research, to improve transplant outcomes for patients with for patients with myelofibrosis and other blood cancers, ultimately enhancing…

img.alt_text: John and Hallie Dovich in Greece

jetpack-related-posts.title: National Marrow Donor Program
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The NMDP provided a $400,000 grant to support the research of Nicoletta Cieri, MD, PhD, at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. This funding will support her work to improve allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation by identifying genetic factors influencing graft-versus-host disease, potentially leading to more personalized treatment strategies and improved patient outcomes.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Swim Across America
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Swim Across America raised $250,000 in 2024 to benefit Dana-Farber’s Perini Family Survivors’ Center. Since 1996, the Boston Open Water Swim has united swimmers of all ages and abilities, raising over $3.5 million in total to support vital survivorship research at Dana-Farber and continuing to “Make Waves Against Cancer.”

jetpack-related-posts.title: $1 million gift fuels survivorship and precision prostate cancer research at Dana-Farber
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: As a child, Donald M. Ephraim, when asked what he wanted to be when he grew up, replied “a philanthropist.” The questioner was impressed with the nobility of the answer.

img.alt_text: Terri Sriberg and Donald M. Ephraim

jetpack-related-posts.title: Richard and Sandra Bornstein
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Sandra Bornstein and her late husband, Richard, made a generous commitment of $400,000 to support early career physician-scientists on the leukemia and stem cell transplant teams at Dana-Farber. Faculty excellence is a top priority of The Dana-Farber Campaign, and this funding will help fuel the growth of promising investigators as they…

img.alt_text: Dana-Farber donors pose for a photo

jetpack-related-posts.title: Back in the saddle again, 2022 PMC raises record $69 million—that’s $900 million since 1980!
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The world can always use more good news, so here is something great—the Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC), the annual bike-a-thon that raises more money for charity than any other single athletic fundraising event in the country, had its best year yet, raising a record $69 million for Dana-Farber in 2022.

Summer 2023
By Colleen Sullivan

3000 Miles to a Cure awarded $100,000 to support the ALLELE-GBM research program at Dana-Farber, under the direction of Keith Ligon, MD, PhD. Ligon’s team is working to put genomic data into the hands of patients, providers, and researchers to advance treatments and clinical trials in glioblastoma (GBM).

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dana-Farber researchers awarded American Society of Hematology funding
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The American Society of Hematology (ASH) funds groundbreaking research on blood and bone marrow disorders. Over the past year, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute researchers have earned a total of $845,000 in competitive ASH grants.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Rally Foundation supports bold pediatric cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Rally Foundation for Childhood Cancer Research recently awarded $450,000 in grants to four Dana-Farber researchers developing innovative treatments for pediatric cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Richard and Eileen Greisch
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Richard and Eileen Greisch made a gift of $100,000 to provide essential resources for melanoma research under the direction of Tamara Sussman, MD. These funds will enable researchers to test novel therapeutics in clinical trials, lead investigations in genomic sequencing, and develop groundbreaking immunotherapeutic approaches.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Ben and Catherine Ivy Foundation helps advance glioblastoma research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Ben and Catherine Ivy Foundation has awarded $524,081 to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute to advance novel immunotherapy approaches to treat glioblastoma.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Defying Cancer 26.2 miles at a time
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On Monday, April 21, more than 500 runners completed the 129th Boston Marathon® as part of the 2025 Dana-Farber Marathon Challenge (DFMC) team.

img.alt_text: Tara and her father in formal attire on her wedding day

jetpack-related-posts.title: Susan G. Komen funds research into new breast cancer treatments
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In its mission to eradicate breast cancer, Susan G. Komen has invested nearly $1.1 billion in research since its founding in 1982. In 2023, Komen continued a longstanding partnership with Dana-Farber by awarding $2.3 million in new grants to Dana-Farber faculty members.

Summer 2023
By Colleen Sullivan
Photography by Sam Ogden

Barbara and Arnold Barron gave $100,000 to support lung cancer research under the direction of Michael Rabin, MD. The couple has supported the work of Rabin and Dana-Farber for many years, this gift marking their latest commitment to spur advancements in durable treatments for lung cancer patients at Dana-Farber and around the globe.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Mindy Green
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With a $100,000 gift, Mindy Green established the Li Li Family EGFR Lung Cancer Research Fund in memory of her mother, Li Li. The fund realizes Li Li’s intention to make a gift to Dana-Farber and will support the cutting-edge research of her thoracic oncologist, Michael Rabin, MD.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Schaubert Family endows visionary fellowship for lung cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: For nearly a decade, the Schaubert family has been a dedicated supporter of lung cancer research at Dana-Farber.

img.alt_text: Eileen Schaubert (center) and her daughters, Suzanne and Amy.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Free ME from Lung Cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Free ME from Lung Cancer Research Fund doubled its impact, matching a previous gift of $100,000 to support research conducted by Jia Luo, MD, in Dana-Farber’s Lowe Center for Thoracic Oncology. The investment will fuel immunotherapy research for patients with an aggressive and underfunded type of lung cancer.

Connolly Small Cell Lung Cancer Research Fund is supporting Jacob Sands, MD, who in collaboration with Matthew Oser, MD, PhD, is exploring new methods to predict…

Tolaney, MD, MPH, received a $100,000 gift from the Connolly Family Fund, established by William and Barbara Connolly, to advance innovative breast cancer research. Their support empowers Tolaney’s team to develop novel strategies for early detection, prevention, and personalized treatment, helping to improve outcomes for…

content.rendered:
Summer 2023
By Casey Reis
Photography by Sam Ogden

The Charles A. King Trust Postdoctoral Research Fellowship Program, administered by Health Resources in Action, awarded grants totaling $246,776 to two Dana-Farber fellows working in small cell lung cancer and leukemia, as part of the trust’s mission to promote the investigation of human disease, to alleviate suffering through improved treatment.

King Trust Postdoctoral Research Fellowship Program, administered by Health Resources in Action, awarded grants totaling $412,400 to support studies into genetic and epigenetic changes that occur in cancer progression, with the goal of identifying new therapeutic targets.

King Trust Postdoctoral Research Fellowship Program, is supporting Sander Lambo, PhD, and Zheqi Li, PhD, with grants totaling $412,400. Lambo’s research seeks to learn more about cell growth pathways of aggressive pediatric brain cancer, while Li studies how protein alterations impact the…

jetpack-related-posts.title: National Cancer Center

jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: National Cancer Center awarded fellowship grants to Dana-Farber totaling $328,000. One new grant will support Katharina Hoebel, MD, PhD, in developing personalized treatment for non-small cell lung cancer through the use of artificial intelligence. With a second new commitment, Diego Martinez Alonso, PhD, will explore how to utilize CDK4/6 inhibitors…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Grants support innovations in pediatric cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: For over 12 years, grants awarded by Hyundai Hope On Wheels® totaling over $5.5 million have supported Dana-Farber investigators and their research to further discovery, leverage new technologies, and revolutionize treatment for pediatric patients everywhere.

content.rendered:
Summer 2023
By Colleen Sullivan

Children’s Cancer Research Fund awarded their Emerging Scientist Award to Dana-Farber pediatric oncologist Emily Heikamp, MD, PhD, MSc. The grant of $100,000 will support Heikamp’s work in uncovering therapeutic vulnerabilities in the NU98-r gene, which could lead to safer and more effective treatments for children with relapsed acute myeloid leukemia.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Cure Childhood Cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s Emily Heikamp, MD, PhD, MSc, received a $220,000 Early Investigator Award from CURE Childhood Cancer. This generous grant supports her research focused on determining whether targeting two proteins can effectively treat a specific type of acute myeloid leukemia. The grant also helps launch her career as an…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Grants support innovations in pediatric cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: For over 12 years, grants awarded by Hyundai Hope On Wheels® totaling over $5.5 million have supported Dana-Farber investigators and their research to further discovery, leverage new technologies, and revolutionize treatment for pediatric patients everywhere.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Damon Runyon supports bold research by emerging talent
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Damon Runyon Cancer Research Foundation has awarded $1.22 million in grants to four early career investigators at Dana-Farber whose research has the potential to yield important breakthroughs in cancer prevention, diagnosis, and treatment.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Rally Foundation supports bold pediatric cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Rally Foundation for Childhood Cancer Research recently awarded $450,000 in grants to four Dana-Farber researchers developing innovative treatments for pediatric cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Charles H. Hood Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Charles H. Hood Foundation awarded Emily Heikamp, MD, PhD, MSc, a generous $200,000 grant to study a combination treatment for acute myeloid leukemia targeting oncogenic fusion proteins and foster her career development as an independent investigator. This funding supports high-risk, high-reward pediatric studies, enabling groundbreaking discoveries, improved care, and…

jetpack-related-posts.title: V Foundation boosts pediatric AML research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The V Foundation is taking aim at acute myeloid leukemia in children with a grant that will enhance Dana-Farber's search for more effective and durable treatments.

Summer 2023
By Colleen Sullivan

Joe Connolly established the Deborah Connolly Small Cell Lung Cancer Research Fund at Dana-Farber in honor of his late wife, with a gift of $100,000. The fund will support research such as studies of the molecular mutations driving small cell lung cancer, with the goal of developing targeted therapies.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Joe Connolly
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Joe Connolly gave $100,000 to fund critical small cell lung cancer research at Dana-Farber. Established in honor of Connolly’s late wife, the Deborah A. Connolly Small Cell Lung Cancer Research Fund is supporting Jacob Sands, MD, who in collaboration with Matthew Oser, MD, PhD, is exploring new methods to predict…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Joseph C. Connolly
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Joseph C. Connolly made a $100,000 gift in memory of his late wife, Deborah, to support the work of Jacob Sands, MD. With this gift, Sands, along with researcher Matthew Oser, MD, PhD, will work to identify biomarkers to personalize treatment and track response to therapy in patients with small…

jetpack-related-posts.title: William and Barbara Connolly
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s Sara M. Tolaney, MD, MPH, received a $100,000 gift from the Connolly Family Fund, established by William and Barbara Connolly, to advance innovative breast cancer research. Their support empowers Tolaney’s team to develop novel strategies for early detection, prevention, and personalized treatment, helping to improve outcomes for…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Mindy Green
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With a $100,000 gift, Mindy Green established the Li Li Family EGFR Lung Cancer Research Fund in memory of her mother, Li Li. The fund realizes Li Li’s intention to make a gift to Dana-Farber and will support the cutting-edge research of her thoracic oncologist, Michael Rabin, MD.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Defeating treatment-resistant lung cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A collaborative, multi-institution team led by Dana-Farber’s David Barbie, MD, received a four-year, $2.5 million grant from the International Association for the Study of Lung Cancer (IASLC) and Lung Cancer Research Foundation (LCRF) for researching a cure for non-small cell lung carcinoma.

img.alt_text: IASLC Lung Cancer Research Foundation logo

jetpack-related-posts.title: Free ME from Lung Cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Free ME from Lung Cancer Research Fund doubled its impact, matching a previous gift of $100,000 to support research conducted by Jia Luo, MD, in Dana-Farber’s Lowe Center for Thoracic Oncology. The investment will fuel immunotherapy research for patients with an aggressive and underfunded type of lung cancer.

img.alt_text: Free ME from Lung Cancer Research Fund logo

Summer 2023
By Colleen Sullivan
Photography by Jessamyn Martin

The Foley Family made a gift of $100,000 to advance research into paragangliomas, a rare type of neuroendocrine tumor, led by Kimberly Perez, MD. Their gift will support experimental studies including the first clinical trial analyzing better treatments for patients with hereditary and non-hereditary paragangliomas.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Novel clinical trial in pancreatic cancer bolstered by $1 million gift
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: John Byrnes is a self-proclaimed “satisfied customer.” Diagnosed with stage IV pancreatic cancer in 2015, John is grateful for each and every day his Dana-Farber care team has given him.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Gift accelerates new treatment possibilities for neuroendocrine tumors
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: An anonymous donor first became acquainted with Dana-Farber Cancer Institute in 2021 through their desire to support the fundraising efforts of a friend

img.alt_text: Liquid pouring from a beaker into a petri dish

jetpack-related-posts.title: Neuroendocrine Tumor Research Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Neuroendocrine Tumor Research Foundation granted a generous $270,000 Investigator Award to Ramesh Shivdasani, MD, PhD, Dana-Farber’s Laurie H. Glimcher, MD, Chair. This funding supports innovative studies to model intestinal neuroendocrine tumor biology, identify therapeutic targets, and bring more treatment options and hope to patients with these complex cancers.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Karen O’Connor and Bruce MacGregor
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Karen O’Connor and Bruce MacGregor made a generous $100,000 commitment, renewing their support of melanoma research under the leadership of Rizwan Haq, MD, PhD. Their impactful philanthropy is driving innovative studies in immunotherapy, including those targeting anti-tumor immunity, aiming to uncover new treatments and improve outcomes for melanoma patients worldwide.

img.alt_text: Three people in a Dana-Farber exam room

jetpack-related-posts.title: Robert and Margaret King
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Robert and Margaret King made a gift of $100,000, supporting melanoma research under the direction of Megan Insco, MD, PhD. Their generous donation advances critical studies in the development of novel therapeutic approaches for the most difficult-to-treat melanomas, while enhancing clinical care for patients affected by this challenging disease.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Gail and Ralph Reynolds
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Gail and Ralph Reynolds made a gift of $100,000 to support the work of Julia Rotow, MD, and Matt Oser, MD, PhD, who are collaborating to pioneer novel treatments for lung neuroendocrine cancer. By harnessing proteins previously considered “undruggable,” they aim to improve options for patients with this complex cancer.

img.alt_text: Various tubes and other lab equipment

Summer 2023
By Shannon Watterson

In September 2022, 24 women stepped into the ring to deliver a knockout against cancer at Haymakers for Hope’s Belles of the Brawl amateur boxing event at MGM Music Hall in Boston’s Fenway area. The bout raised $116,000 for Dana-Farber and gave women who have been affected by cancer an opportunity to fight back.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Kicks for Cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Each September, the Concord-Carlisle High School community in Concord, Mass., comes together for Kicks for Cancer, an opportunity for area high school sports teams to support Dr.  Dipanjan Chowdhury's Ovarian Cancer Early Detection Fund. The 2022 event raised $116,000 for Dana-Farber and honored students’ loved ones who have faced cancer.

img.alt_text: Two soccer players at the Kicks for Cancer event

jetpack-related-posts.title: 2025 PMC Winter Cycle
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC), the nation’s single most successful athletic fundraiser and Dana-Farber’s largest single contributor, kicked off its 2025 fundraising year at the 10th PMC Winter Cycle on Feb. 1 at Fenway Park.

img.alt_text: Bikers on stationary bikes at the PMC Winter Cycle event

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jimmy Fund Day at Fenway
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Jimmy Fund Day at Fenway presented by DraftKings raised $230,000 to support innovative cancer research and compassionate patient care at Dana-Farber. Thanks to donor support, Dana-Farber patients and their families were able to participate in this unforgettable experience and take the field at Fenway Park.

img.alt_text: Jimmy Fund Day at Fenway logo

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jimmy Fund Day at Fenway
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In September 2025, dreams became reality as more than 200 participants, including Dana-Farber patients, had the once-in-a lifetime chance to play ball at Fenway Park. Thanks to generous support from sponsors, the Boston Red Sox, fundraising teams, and donors, Jimmy Fund Day at Fenway presented by DraftKings raised more than…

img.alt_text: Three people at Fenway Park wearing Jimmy Fund jerseys

jetpack-related-posts.title: Defy cancer celebration
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Defy Cancer Celebration at Fenway Park on Sunday, March 30, was a day filled with hope, progress, and community. It highlighted the impact and innovation in cancer care and research made possible by gifts to The Dana-Farber Campaign from 2017 to 2024.

img.alt_text: People at Fenway Park during the Defy Cancer celebration event

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon breaks records with $5.7 million raised for Dana-Farber
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The WEEI/NESN Jimmy Fund Radio-Telethon presented by Arbella Insurance continued to be a beacon of support for Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund in August with a record-breaking fundraising year.

img.alt_text: Ali Kelleher cheering at Fenway Park

content.rendered:
Summer 2023
By Shannon Watterson
Photography by John Straggas

Each September, the Concord-Carlisle High School community in Concord, Mass., comes together for Kicks for Cancer, an opportunity for area high school sports teams to support Dr.  Dipanjan Chowdhury’s Ovarian Cancer Early Detection Fund. The 2022 event raised $116,000 for Dana-Farber and honored students’ loved ones who have faced cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Kicks for Cancer celebrates record-setting year
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Each year since 2007, Kicks for Cancer has brought together athletes and fans from Concord-Carlisle High School and 17 surrounding towns to raise funds for ovarian cancer research at Dana-Farber.

img.alt_text: Young soccer players in bright pink shirts

jetpack-related-posts.title: Kicks for Cancer harnesses power of community to drive cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Nearly 20 years ago, Concord-Carlisle High School hosted its first Kicks for Cancer soccer match to honor the memory of Lois Wells, the mother of assistant men’s soccer coach Steve Wells, who passed away from ovarian cancer. Today, Kicks for Cancer has grown into a vibrant week-long celebration that unites…

img.alt_text: Soccer players mid-game on the field

jetpack-related-posts.title: Haymakers for Hope
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In September 2022, 24 women stepped into the ring to deliver a knockout against cancer at Haymakers for Hope’s Belles of the Brawl amateur boxing event at MGM Music Hall in Boston’s Fenway area. The bout raised $116,000 for Dana-Farber and gave women who have been affected by cancer an…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Svanberg family establishes endowed chair with focus on early detection
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dipanjan Chowdhury, PhD, was named the inaugural incumbent of the prestigious Svanberg Family Chair at Dana-Farber, which was endowed to provide perpetual support for research into early detection and prevention of cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Gray Foundation empowers team science against BRCA-mutated cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Philanthropy has transformative power to address society’s intractable challenges. The Gray Foundation is committed to this goal and, with two grants totaling nearly $6 million, is harnessing this power for good through The Dana-Farber Campaign.

jetpack-related-posts.title: V is for victory over intractable cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The V Foundation for Cancer Research, founded by legendary basketball coach Jim Valvano, has granted $1.6 million to four Dana-Farber investigators.

By Kayla Stravin
Photography by Josh Campbell

The Mulligan Family organized a birthday fundraiser for Dana-Farber in honor of their loved one, Patrick. They raised over $15,000 to help James Cleary, MD, PhD, standardize screening options and uncover more effective treatments for pancreatic cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Yoseph Linde
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Yoseph Linde renewed his support of Dana-Farber with a recent gift of $100,000 to advance bile duct cancer research under the direction of James Cleary, MD, PhD. This latest gift, in honor of his late wife Haya, supports Cleary’s team’s continued in-depth DNA and RNA sequencing work to better understand…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Lustgarten Foundation invests $1.5 million to bring promising immunotherapy to patients with pancreatic cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: When the Lustgarten Foundation was founded in 1998, fewer than 10 principal investigators across the U.S. had a primary focus on pancreatic cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Kevin and Kimberley Mitnick
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Kevin and Kimberley Mitnick made a generous gift to support pancreatic cancer research by Srivatsan Raghavan, MD, PhD, before Kevin’s passing from pancreatic cancer in July 2023. This generous contribution reflects their desire to help Dana-Farber uncover new treatment options and improve outcomes for all patients facing pancreatic cancer.

img.alt_text: Kevin and Kimberley Mitnick sitting on a rock in front of the ocean

jetpack-related-posts.title: Brenda McAdam
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: After being diagnosed with cholangiocarcinoma, a rare bile duct cancer, in August 2022, Brenda McAdam established the Brenda McAdam Fund for Bile Duct Cancer Research at Dana-Farber under the direction of James Cleary, MD, PhD. With her $100,000 gift, she hopes Cleary can help patients like her defy this rare…

img.alt_text: A closeup photo of a couple

jetpack-related-posts.title: Michael and Margaret Kerr
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Michael and Margaret Kerr established the Kerr Family Fund for Translational Research at Dana-Farber with a $100,000 gift in 2023. The fund will be directed by James Cleary, MD, PhD, whom the couple laud for his compassionate patient care.

img.alt_text: A photo of two people outside on a balcony

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Campaign: Stopping cancer before it starts
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Dana-Farber Campaign dramatically advanced the prevention, early detection, and interception of cancers on a wide variety of fronts.

img.alt_text: Researchers at work in the Centers for Early Detection and Interception.

One Mission, founded in 2008 by Ashley and Ari Haseotes, aims to help families cope with the emotional and financial challenges brought on by childhood cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: One Mission
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In 2023, One Mission contributed $189,000 to Dana-Farber, reinforcing its long-standing dedication to pediatric cancer patients. This contribution enhances the wellbeing of young patients through the Pediatric Resource Program as well as family-centered initiatives like the Jimmy Fund Clinic Festival, a Parent Bereavement cruise, and other special events for patients…

jetpack-related-posts.title: HomeGoods expands support to enhance patient care
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Through HomeGoods’ Find Home Anywhere mission—funded largely by donations from its generous shoppers—HomeGoods and the TJX Foundation have made a three-year commitment to donate at least $3.6 million to Dana-Farber.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Rallying to defy pediatric cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Bolstering Dana-Farber’s mission to defy cancer, Rally Foundation for Childhood Cancer Research made grants totaling $850,000 in 2023 to help drive much-needed progress in pediatric oncology research.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Stop & Shop raises over $760,000 for pediatric cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: This spring, New England Stop & Shop customers donated over $760,000 to pediatric cancer research at Dana-Farber through the grocery chain’s annual Help Cure Childhood Cancer campaign.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Together in action, together in progress: Giving Day surpasses fundraising goal
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: This year’s annual Giving Day marked an especially generous occasion for dedicated supporters of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Cookies for Kids’ Cancer funds groundbreaking Dana-Farber pediatric cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Cookies for Kids’ Cancer has awarded two grants totaling $600,000 to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute to support groundbreaking pediatric cancer research.

title.rendered: Rally Foundation for Childhood Cancer Research

content.rendered:
Summer 2023
By Colleen Sullivan

The Rally Foundation for Childhood Cancer Research awarded $300,000 in grants to support exploring liquid biopsies to advance precision treatment; uncovering causes of drug resistance in relapsed neuroblastoma; analyzing the proteins that drive medulloblastoma; and testing nanoparticle delivery of targeted therapy in diffuse midline gliomas to lay the groundwork for clinical trials.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Cookies for Kids’ Cancer funds groundbreaking Dana-Farber pediatric cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Cookies for Kids’ Cancer has awarded two grants totaling $600,000 to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute to support groundbreaking pediatric cancer research.

jetpack-related-posts.title: V Foundation spurs pivotal research aimed at new epigenetic therapies
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The V Foundation is spurring Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s efforts to eradicate difficult-to-treat cancers through recent grants totaling $1.6 million awarded to two Dana-Farber investigators who aim to develop novel treatments known as epigenetic therapies.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Sontag Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Sontag Foundation has generously donated $100,000 to Mariella Filbin, MD, PhD, to support her groundbreaking research on diffuse midline gliomas (DMG). Her project aims to uncover how neuronal interactions contribute to radio resistance in DMG, potentially leading to novel therapeutic strategies for enhancing radiation efficacy.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Rally Foundation supports bold pediatric cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Rally Foundation for Childhood Cancer Research recently awarded $450,000 in grants to four Dana-Farber researchers developing innovative treatments for pediatric cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: St. Baldrick’s Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: St. Baldrick’s Foundation awarded a total of $415,000 to Dana-Farber studies into how neuroblastoma, one of the most common pediatric solid tumors, escapes destruction by the immune system; and how a category of newly discovered “dark proteins” may point toward new approaches to treat medulloblastoma, a devastating form of childhood…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Alex’s Lemonade Stand Foundation grants millions to advance childhood cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: It all began over 20 years ago with a simple, yet profound, act of kindness by Alex Scott, a determined little girl with cancer, who held a lemonade stand fundraiser to help other kids like her and inspired countless others to do the same.

title.rendered: Richard and Susan Smith Family Foundation

content.rendered:
Summer 2023
By Katherine Agate

A $300,000 Odyssey Award from the Richard and Susan Smith Family Foundation provides critical resources to develop a groundbreaking platform to analyze the structure and function of disordered proteins that drive disease progression. This pioneering project promises to reveal structural biological insights while validating a powerful new tool to inform drug discovery across multiple cancers.

jetpack-related-posts.title: $10 million gift brings rare cancers to the fore
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Linde Family Foundation has made a transformative $10 million gift to Dana-Farber to launch the Center for Therapeutic Discovery, which will develop novel therapies for patients with rare and hard-to-treat cancers.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Richard and Susan Smith Family receives Institute’s highest honor, the Sidney Farber Medical Research Award
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On a beautiful evening in mid-September, members of the Dana-Farber community gathered to celebrate the presentation of the 2022 Sidney Farber Medical Research Award to the Richard and Susan Smith Family.

img.alt_text: Debra Smith Knez; Institute Trustee Amy Smith Berylson; Laurie H. Glimcher, MD; Robert A. Smith; and Dana-Farber Chairman of the Board Josh Bekenstein

jetpack-related-posts.title: Advancing Parkinson’s research: Spiegelman’s groundbreaking work
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: From a remarkable act of generosity, the Tyler Family has donated $3 million to establish the Tyler Family Fund for Parkinson's Research, supporting the groundbreaking work of Bruce Spiegelman, PhD, the Stanley J. Korsmeyer, MD, Professor of Cell Biology and Medicine at Harvard Medical School.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Groundbreaking studies take aim at disparities and advanced disease
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Prostate Cancer Foundation (PCF) has awarded grants totaling more than $2.3 million to Dana-Farber researchers.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Breast Cancer Research Foundation grants more than $4 million to speed Dana-Farber research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Building on past support, BCRF recently made grants totaling more than $4 million to 12 physician-scientists at Dana-Farber.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The DeGregorio Family Foundation continues to advance gastroesophageal cancer treatment
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Gastric and esophageal cancers often resist chemotherapy and metastasize easily. The DeGregorio Family Foundation aims to address this challenge with more than $500,000 in grant funding to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute to develop new treatments.

content.rendered:
Summer 2023
By Colleen Sullivan
Photography by Michael Blanchard

The Samuel Waxman Cancer Research Foundation awarded $200,000 to Dana-Farber to support research into how aging affects the behavior of tumor cells. This research, led by Lewis Cantley, PhD, in the Department of Cancer Biology, could provide further insight that may inform the development of age-specific treatment approaches for cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Mathers Foundation grants promote basic cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Many of today’s important advances in cancer care trace their origins to basic research—a form of scientific investigation aimed at uncovering the fundamental principles of biology, chemistry, and foundational science.

jetpack-related-posts.title: AACR grants support sarcoma, renal cell carcinoma, and cancer biology research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The American Association for Cancer Research (AACR) recently awarded $580,000 to three Dana-Farber physician-scientists who are investigating new methods of prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of various types of cancers. As the first cancer research organization dedicated to preventing and curing cancer, AACR is a long-standing partner in Dana-Farber’s mission to…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Hard-to-treat cancers are focus of Cancer Research Institute grants
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Cancer Research Institute (CRI) has awarded nearly $1.5 million in grants to Dana-Farber in support of investigations into how immunotherapy can be used to defeat difficult-to-treat and incurable cancers

jetpack-related-posts.title: Lustgarten grant accelerates therapeutic discovery in pancreatic cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Lustgarten Foundation is the largest private funder of pancreatic cancer research in the world, funding preeminent pancreatic cancer researchers, driving the pursuit of bold and innovative science toward earlier detection and better treatments, and transforming pancreatic cancer into a curable disease.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Edward P. Evans Foundation grants propel MDS research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Edward P. Evans Foundation, which funds the most promising research in myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS), a type of blood cancer, has awarded grants totaling $2.325 million to five Dana-Farber researchers who are pursuing innovative MDS strategies.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Mark Foundation spurs innovation in immunotherapy
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Mark Foundation for Cancer Research has awarded Dana-Farber investigator Catherine Wu, MD, and two investigators at the Broad Institute a $3 million, three-year grant to further their research into personalized, T cell-directed cancer immunotherapy.

content.rendered:
Summer 2023
By Colleen Sullivan

St. Baldrick’s Foundation awarded a total of $415,000 to Dana-Farber studies into how neuroblastoma, one of the most common pediatric solid tumors, escapes destruction by the immune system; and how a category of newly discovered “dark proteins” may point toward new approaches to treat medulloblastoma, a devastating form of childhood brain cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: St. Baldrick’s Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: St. Baldrick’s Foundation has awarded grants totaling $395,000 to fund pediatric cancer research by Institute researchers Rahela Aziz-Bose, MD, and Jun Qi, PhD. The grants will support their research to better understand and tackle barriers to nutrition for childhood cancer survivors and identify novel targets for pediatric brain tumors and…

jetpack-related-posts.title: St. Baldrick’s Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: St. Baldrick’s Foundation renewed their support for Dana-Farber with grants totaling nearly $200,000 to fund studies that will lay the groundwork for better precision medicine approaches for children with leukemia. These projects, led by Dana-Farber, involve collaboration with multiple institutions in the U.S. and abroad.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dana-Farber faculty are part of “grand challenge” to defeat childhood tumors
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber has been awarded more than $3 million in funding as part of a Cancer Grand Challenge to find new treatments for solid tumors in children.

jetpack-related-posts.title: V Foundation spurs pivotal research aimed at new epigenetic therapies
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The V Foundation is spurring Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s efforts to eradicate difficult-to-treat cancers through recent grants totaling $1.6 million awarded to two Dana-Farber investigators who aim to develop novel treatments known as epigenetic therapies.

jetpack-related-posts.title: PBTF Speeds pursuit of more effective pediatric brain tumor treatments
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Pediatric Brain Tumor Foundation is accelerating Dana-Farber research into pediatric low-grade gliomas, most common brain tumors in children.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Cookies for Kids’ Cancer funds groundbreaking Dana-Farber pediatric cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Cookies for Kids’ Cancer has awarded two grants totaling $600,000 to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute to support groundbreaking pediatric cancer research.

By Katherine Agate
Photography by Michael Blanchard

Tap Cancer Out, a jiu-jitsu based nonprofit raising awareness and funds for cancer fighting organizations on behalf of the grappling community, recently made a $100,000 gift to support innovative research by Rizwan Romee, MD, into novel immunotherapeutic approaches for breast cancer at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Richard and Eileen Greisch
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Richard and Eileen Greisch made a gift of $100,000 to provide essential resources for melanoma research under the direction of Tamara Sussman, MD. These funds will enable researchers to test novel therapeutics in clinical trials, lead investigations in genomic sequencing, and develop groundbreaking immunotherapeutic approaches.

jetpack-related-posts.title: William and Barbara Connolly
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s Sara M. Tolaney, MD, MPH, received a $100,000 gift from the Connolly Family Fund, established by William and Barbara Connolly, to advance innovative breast cancer research. Their support empowers Tolaney’s team to develop novel strategies for early detection, prevention, and personalized treatment, helping to improve outcomes for…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Melanoma Research Alliance
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Since its founding in 2007, the Melanoma Research Alliance has become the largest nonprofit funder of crucial melanoma research worldwide. In 2025, they awarded $430,000 in grants to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute supporting the work of Rizwan Haq, MD, PhD, Giacomo Oliveira, PhD, and David Liu, MD, MPH, MS, to advance…

jetpack-related-posts.title: American Cancer Society grants propel research and programs forward
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The American Cancer Society (ACS) recently awarded more than $3.1 million in grants to 11 Dana-Farber Cancer Institute investigators. These grants support various areas across Dana-Farber, including research on improved outcomes and patient assistance programming to help with access to care.

jetpack-related-posts.title: PopStroke
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: PopStroke completed its second annual October Breast Cancer Awareness Initiative, last year, in partnership with Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund. Throughout October, PopStroke locations nationally ran a number of initiatives to support breast cancer research and patient care at Dana-Farber, raising close to $145,000.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Phyllis and Richard Krock
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Institute Trustee Phyllis Krock and her husband, Richard, gave a generous gift of $100,000 to the Palm Beach Initiative. The funds are dedicated to the Presidential Initiatives Fund under Dana-Farber President and CEO Benjamin L. Ebert, MD, PhD. With this support, Dana-Farber physicians and researchers can continue developing innovative cancer…

title.rendered: $10 million gift brings rare cancers to the fore

content.rendered:
Summer 2023
By Kathy Clute
Photography by Sam Ogden, Bryce Vickmark

The Linde Family Foundation has made a transformative $10 million gift to Dana-Farber to launch the Center for Therapeutic Discovery, which will develop novel therapies for patients with rare and hard-to-treat cancers. 

“Drug discovery for rare cancers often goes unaddressed because the market is perceived to be too small,” said Scott Armstrong, MD, PhD, who co-directs the new center with Eric Fischer, PhD. “This generous support from the Linde Family Foundation allows Dana-Farber to invest in novel therapeutic projects with a focus on impact, not profit, delivering new options and hope for patients facing the toughest cancers.” Accelerating drug development is a key strategic priority of The Dana-Farber Campaign.

Investigators across Dana-Farber will be invited to submit their most promising drug candidates to the new center for focused funding and expert support. Each year, the center’s staff and its distinguished advisory panel will select two to five projects to be shepherded through the preclinical pipeline and further toward clinical trials. Drug candidates will be chosen based on their ability to address pediatric and adult cancers with poor treatment outcomes.

“This level of funding and expertise is rare in academic medicine,” said Laurie H. Glimcher, president and CEO of Dana-Farber and the Richard and Susan Smith Professor of Medicine. “With the resources and know-how provided by the team at the Center for Therapeutic Discovery, our scientists’ most significant breakthroughs can advance from the bench to the bedside for the benefit of patients everywhere. We are so grateful for the Linde family’s partnership in this pioneering venture.”

This latest gift, and the center it launched, builds on the family’s prior support of the Institute’s Chemical Biology Program and the Department of Pediatric Oncology.

“Dana-Farber is a leader in innovation and drug discovery,” said Karen Linde Packman, Dana-Farber Trustee and a member of The Dana-Farber Campaign Cabinet. “It is our hope that this gift will bring discoveries even closer to the clinic, leading to new treatments for pediatric and adult cancers.”

The new center is a strategic priority for Dana-Farber, which expects to invest $40 million—from philanthropic and Institute resources—in the venture during the next five years. The Linde Family Foundation stands ready to provide an additional $5 million grant to support the center if the Institute reaches specific milestones.

“It is our hope that this gift will lead to new treatments for pediatric and adult cancers.”

Karen Linde Packman, Linde Family Foundation

The center’s co-directors are two of Dana-Farber’s leaders in drug discovery. Armstrong, who chairs the Department of Pediatric Oncology and is the David G. Nathan, MD, Professor of Pediatrics, has made seminal discoveries into the causes of pediatric leukemia and the epigenetic mechanisms that lead to cancer in children. Fischer is director of Dana-Farber’s Chemical Biology Program and a world-renowned expert in cutting-edge approaches to structural and chemical biology, including targeted protein degradation.

excerpt.rendered: The Linde Family Foundation has made a transformative $10 million gift to Dana-Farber to launch the Center for Therapeutic Discovery, which will develop novel therapies for patients with rare and hard-to-treat cancers.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Harrington Discovery Institute
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With a generous $460,000 contribution, the Harrington Discovery Institute is propelling innovative cancer research led by Min-Ru Wu, MD, PhD, and Loren Walensky, MD, PhD, as they work to develop less toxic treatments for melanoma patients and investigate targeted therapies for other drug-resistant cancers, respectively.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Robert and Margaret King
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Robert and Margaret King made a gift of $100,000, supporting melanoma research under the direction of Megan Insco, MD, PhD. Their generous donation advances critical studies in the development of novel therapeutic approaches for the most difficult-to-treat melanomas, while enhancing clinical care for patients affected by this challenging disease.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Expect Miracles Foundation continues to drive discovery
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: For the 29th year, Expect Miracles Foundation reaffirmed their support of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute with a gift of $1 million.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Neuroendocrine Tumor Research Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Neuroendocrine Tumor Research Foundation granted a generous $270,000 Investigator Award to Ramesh Shivdasani, MD, PhD, Dana-Farber’s Laurie H. Glimcher, MD, Chair. This funding supports innovative studies to model intestinal neuroendocrine tumor biology, identify therapeutic targets, and bring more treatment options and hope to patients with these complex cancers.

jetpack-related-posts.title: What is basic science?
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The first step in creating cutting-edge cancer treatments for patients is basic research—scientific investigation that uncovers biology’s fundamental principles and helps us understand how the cells and molecules in our bodies work.

jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Leukemia & Lymphoma Society (LLS) has awarded six grants totaling $5.8 million to Dana-Farber investigators.

By Robbie Merritt
Photography by Josh Campbell, John Deputy, Steve McLaughlin, Rachel O’Driscoll/Boston Red Sox, Pan-Mass Challenge, Bryce Vickmark

On May 22, 1948, Einar Gustafson, a young boy being treated for lymphoma by Dr. Sidney Farber and dubbed “Jimmy” to protect his privacy, shared his story from his hospital bed. The radio broadcast, organized by the Variety Children’s Charity of New England, inspired more than $200,000 in donations from across the country. That generous community of donors, who first rallied together to raise money for a TV (pictured) so Jimmy could watch baseball, is what became known, fondly, as the Jimmy Fund.

“As we mark the Jimmy Fund’s 75-year anniversary, we take pride in remaining anchored by the core principles of Dr. Sidney Farber’s mission: to make scientific discoveries and turn them into lifesaving treatments,” said Laurie H. Glimcher, MD, Dana-Farber president and CEO. “The Jimmy Fund has enabled Dana-Farber to become one of the world’s leading centers of cancer research and treatment, saving countless lives.”

While it has grown considerably over the last 75 years—becoming the official charity partner of the Pan-Mass Challenge, Boston Red Sox, the Variety Children’s Charity of New England, and the Massachusetts Chiefs of Police Association—the Jimmy Fund has remained a community: A grassroots movement of people of all ages and backgrounds, organizing events and participating in programs—such as this year’s Giving Day on May 22—solely dedicated to raising money for cancer research and patient care at Dana-Farber.

In the decades since Jimmy’s original broadcast, the generosity of millions all over the world has helped the Jimmy Fund directly support Dana-Farber’s mission of turning groundbreaking research into lifesaving treatments to defy cancer, for patients of all ages.

“I’m continuously impressed by the resilience and dedication of the entire Jimmy Fund community,” said Larry Lucchino, Chairman of the Jimmy Fund. “What we’ve been able to accomplish together over 75 years for cancer research and care at Dana-Farber—the benefits of which I have experienced firsthand—is nothing short of monumental.”

Since 1947, when Sidney Farber, MD, completed the first successful treatment of blood cancer using chemotherapy, Dana-Farber has remained on the cutting edge of bench-to-bedside research and high-quality, total patient care. Today, breakthroughs continue thanks to support from the Jimmy Fund community, leading to new and innovative cancer therapies that change the way the world treats cancer.

“As the original ‘Jimmy,’ Dad was so proud to be able to show people that if he was able to make it based on the research and medicines available in 1948, with how improved it is today because of all the donations, that you could make it, too,” said Einar Gustafson’s daughters, Lynn MacLeod and Lisa Patti. “He wanted to show people hope. That was his legacy: hope.”

Together, we have continued Dr. Farber’s promise to never accept the incurability of cancer. Together, we celebrate 75 years of progress, impact, and dedication to creating a more hopeful, cancer-free future. Together, we’re all Jimmy, and we will continue to defy cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Message from Melany Duval
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: When Dr. Sidney Farber achieved the first remissions in childhood leukemia in 1947, he changed everything.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Jimmy Fund: 75 years of impact
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Since the seminal radio broadcast in 1948 that introduced the nation to a young cancer patient dubbed “Jimmy” and the researchers and clinicians dedicated to caring for children with cancer, the Jimmy Fund’s generous community of supporters has contributed an incredible total of more than $1.5 billion so far.

img.alt_text: Patient Navigator Marlene Escobar and Vice President of Community Health Magnolia Contreras are pictured outside of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Message from Melany Duval
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: It all started in 1948 with a 12-year-old boy with cancer dubbed “Jimmy,” who inspired thousands to give money in support of cancer research.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Your generosity soars past $2 million on GivingTuesday
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On GivingTuesday 2024, Dana-Farber and the Jimmy Fund’s community of support far surpassed our $1 million goal.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Meet the new Co-Chairs of the Jimmy Fund: Brock Holt and Tom Caron
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Holt and Caron will be the lead ambassadors and public spokespeople on behalf of the Jimmy Fund, helping to raise funds and awareness.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Chairmen of the Jimmy Fund: building community since 1948
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Since the earliest days of the Jimmy Fund, passionate and committed individuals have devoted their time, talents, resources, and relationships to raising money in support of a powerful possibility: curing cancer for everyone.
