title.rendered: Palm Beach surpasses $67 million in gifts to The Dana-Farber Campaign

content.rendered:
Summer 2023
By Samantha Eisenberg
Photography by Capehart Photography

For over three decades, the compassionate community in Palm Beach, Florida, has provided generous support for Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s lifesaving mission to conquer cancer in adults and children—not only in Boston and Palm Beach, but also across the country and around the world.

That’s why, as part of The Dana-Farber Campaign, visionary Palm Beach donors set ambitious goals to both raise $60 million and increase membership in the Dana-Farber Society, a special group whose legacy gifts help secure the Institute’s future progress. Through the generosity and commitment of those in Palm Beach, over $67 million has been raised to date, and a record number of new donors joined the Dana-Farber Society.

As The Dana-Farber Campaign continues, our steadfast Palm Beach community remains dedicated to raising funds for campaign priorities including progress for early detection, expanding access and care to underserved patient populations, and advancing transformative research.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Palm Beach Annual Appeal again surpasses its goal
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Year after year, the Palm Beach community demonstrates their unwavering commitment to Dana-Farber in many ways including through the Palm Beach Annual Appeal.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Palm Beach Annual Leadership Dinner
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber’s Palm Beach Annual Leadership Dinner was held in March, recognizing the most generous donors in the community to the Palm Beach Annual Appeal and The Dana-Farber Campaign.

img.alt_text: Phyllis Krock and Laurie H. Glimcher

jetpack-related-posts.title: Palm Beach community rallies to surpass annual fundraising goal
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Palm Beach community once again demonstrated remarkable generosity by raising over $1.31 million to support Dana-Farber Cancer Institute through their Palm Beach Annual appeal.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Over $1 million raised from 2023 Palm Beach Annual Appeal
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Each year, the Palm Beach community generously comes together to raise funds for Dana-Farber.

img.alt_text: Phyllis and Richard Krock at the Palm Beach Annual Appeal

jetpack-related-posts.title: Phyllis and Richard Krock
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Institute Trustee Phyllis Krock and her husband, Richard, gave a generous gift of $100,000 to the Palm Beach Initiative. The funds are dedicated to the Presidential Initiatives Fund under Dana-Farber President and CEO Benjamin L. Ebert, MD, PhD. With this support, Dana-Farber physicians and researchers can continue developing innovative cancer…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Ravestock Boston
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Ravestock Boston, hosted in October by the William Raveis Charitable Fund, raised nearly $150,000 for Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s life-changing mission. Held in memory of Meghan Raveis, the event brought together community and live music to benefit Dana-Farber's cancer research and care, while honoring Meghan’s legacy of service to others.

title.rendered: Mathers Foundation grants promote basic cancer research

content.rendered:
Summer 2023
By Scott Edwards
Photography by Bryce Vickmark

Many of today’s important advances in cancer care trace their origins to basic research—a form of scientific investigation aimed at uncovering the fundamental principles of biology, chemistry, and foundational science. With grants totaling $2.25 million from the G. Harold & Leila Y. Mathers Charitable Foundation, three Dana-Farber scientists are pursuing novel basic research studies that may set the foundation for new cancer treatments.

Wayne Marasco, MD, PhD, is probing a novel cellular mechanism to attack tumors. He is exploring a new form of cellular therapy known as chimeric antibody signaling and secreting (CASS) B cells. These cells are engineered to recognize tumor-specific antigens through a receptor that activates CASS B cells and induces the production of elevated levels of antibodies to attack the tumor.

“The idea of engineering human B cells to seek out cancer cells and secrete these antibodies at the tumor site is novel and untested, and could provide a new way to treat both primary and metastatic tumors,” says Marasco.

In her lab, Evanna Mills, PhD, is exploring how metabolites control brown fat to reduce obesity, which is a risk factor for cancer. Brown and beige fat have an abundance of macrophages—white blood cells that eliminate damaged and diseased cells—which play a role in the regulation of fat cells. She is studying mechanisms by which itaconate, a metabolite produced by macrophages that controls inflammatory responses, regulates brown and beige fat cell function and anti-obesity activity.

While chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy, which uses specially altered T cells to reprogram patients’ immune systems to target cancer cells, has been successful in certain blood cancers, these modified cells do not last in the body forever. To address this issue, Eric Smith, MD, PhD, director of translational research for the Immune Effector Cell Therapy Program at Dana-Farber, is developing approaches that will, in patients, continuously generate immune cells expressing a CAR—a special receptor created in the lab that binds to certain proteins on cancer cells—to target and eliminate cancer cells. His work could have important implications for gene therapy and cellular therapy to treat blood cancers.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Basic research is focus of Mathers Charitable Foundation grants
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The G. Harold and Leila Y. Mathers Charitable Foundation has awarded Dana-Farber $1.47 million to support two Institute researchers investigating how cancer develops and how cells detect and respond to viral infections.

jetpack-related-posts.title: High-risk, high-reward research is The Mathers Foundation’s priority
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Transformative basic research is the focus of The G. Harold and Leila Y. Mathers Charitable Foundation, which recently awarded $1.5 million to fund Dana-Farber research on unraveling the inner workings of human cells.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Damon Runyon Cancer Research Foundation invests in tomorrow’s discoveries
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber received over $3,156,000 in grants from the Damon Runyon Cancer Research Foundation in 2024 supporting 10 physician-scientists and researchers.

jetpack-related-posts.title: What is basic science?
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The first step in creating cutting-edge cancer treatments for patients is basic research—scientific investigation that uncovers biology’s fundamental principles and helps us understand how the cells and molecules in our bodies work.

img.alt_text: Close-up photo of a researcher looking through a microscope

jetpack-related-posts.title: Trustee Science Committee fosters the next generation of researchers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Shelby Roseman, PhD, and Amanda Smythers, PhD, were recently named the latest group of Trustee Science Committee Postdoctoral Fellows at Dana-Farber.

img.alt_text: Liquid pouring from a beaker into a petri dish

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Message from Melany Duval
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Science has long been the catalyst for transformative cancer care. More recently, we’ve witnessed revolutionary advances that have benefited patients and those who hold them dear.

title.rendered: Endowed fellowship looks to the future

content.rendered:
Summer 2023
By Stephanie Lowitt

Baila Janock embodies generosity in its many forms. For over 30 years, she has combined her gifts of time, treasure, and talent to make a long-lasting impact on Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and its patients. She has been an Institute volunteer, platelet donor, and captain of Team Irv in the Boston Marathon® Jimmy Fund Walk. And as one of the founding members of the Dana-Farber Society, a special community of donors who include Dana-Farber and the Jimmy Fund in their estate plans, she has ensured that the critical research and treatment she cares about are funded well past her lifetime.

Recently, Janock generously pledged $1 million to establish the Baila A. Janock Fellowship Fund to support a fellowship focused on pancreatic cancer. Fellowships like this attract the brightest minds in the field and prepare a new generation of physicians and scientists to become tomorrow’s leaders in clinical and laboratory investigation and patient care.

“Baila has been a phenomenal champion of our early career faculty,” said Robert Mayer, MD, faculty vice president for academic affairs at Dana-Farber and the Stephen B. Kay Family Professor of Medicine, who led the Fellowship Program in Hematology/Oncology for 35 years. “Since 1996, 25 of these extremely talented individuals have had the good fortune to be Janock Fellows. Many of them have developed lasting relationships with her. Baila’s continued support of Dana-Farber and our gastrointestinal cancer program in particular has been simply extraordinary.”

“It was important to me that Dana-Farber receive a significant gift from my estate. It is a privilege to be a part of the Dana-Farber family.”

Baila Janock

In addition, Janock made a significant gift to fuel capital projects and strategic initiatives that will be recognized with a named space, linking her generosity in a tangible way to the Institute’s lifesaving mission. To Baila, this physical representation of her legacy provides an opportunity to show others how their support could also change lives now and into the future.

Janock’s reasons for making gifts through her estate are numerous. For her, it was important that a fellowship would continue in perpetuity and that she could reduce future estate taxes. She valued the peace of mind she gained from deciding now about the legacy she would leave. “Giving during my lifetime has always been important to me, and I want to continue doing so after my death,” she says. “It was important to me that Dana-Farber receive a significant gift from my estate. The Institute has always been my home away from home and it is a privilege to be a part of the Dana-Farber family. I receive far more than I could possibly give financially.”

title.rendered: V is for victory over intractable cancers

content.rendered:
Summer 2023
By Jodi Hyer
Photography by Sam Ogden

The V Foundation for Cancer Research, founded by legendary basketball coach Jim Valvano, has granted $1.6 million to four Dana-Farber investigators conducting innovative research aimed at improving early detection and overcoming treatment resistance for a variety of challenging cancers.

Dipanjan Chowdhury, PhD, and Srinivas Viswanathan, MD, PhD, are using their V Foundation awards for research that could lead to new methods of early detection, interception, and prevention. Chowdhury, the Svanberg Family Chair at Dana-Farber, is developing a microRNA-based blood test to identify individuals at elevated risk of developing ovarian and breast cancers and to predict when their cancer could occur. This test could revolutionize early detection and dramatically improve survival, particularly for ovarian cancer, which is usually not treated until late, advanced stages since no early diagnostic test exists.

Viswanathan is studying translocation renal cell carcinoma (tRCC), a rare, often misdiagnosed form of kidney cancer, to establish a new detection method based on its unique gene expression pattern. This work aims to uncover tRCC’s key molecular characteristics and advance the accuracy and ease of diagnosis, which could facilitate earlier interventions that may cure this aggressive cancer before it spreads.

In the realm of innovating new and improved therapies, Pratiti (Mimi) Bandopadhayay, MBBS, PhD, and Mark Awad, MD, PhD, are dedicating their efforts to some of the most challenging and drug-resistant cancers—childhood gliomas and non-small cell lung carcinoma (NSCLC), respectively. Gliomas are the most common cause of cancer-related death in children, and treatment options remain limited. With the goal of finding new targeted therapies for this devastating disease, Bandopadhayay will use her V Foundation award to determine how FGFR gene mutations cooperate with other activating mutations to drive pediatric gliomas. This research aims to identify new genetic targets for combination therapies that will enhance the effectiveness of FGFR inhibitors and overcome FGFR-inhibitor drug resistance which occurs commonly in patients with glioma.

Awad, clinical director of the Thoracic Oncology Treatment Center at Dana-Farber, is developing a cancer vaccine for ALK-mutated NSCLC in patients whose cancer has developed resistance to ALK-inhibitor drugs. Although these drugs are initially effective, the cancer frequently becomes resistant, leaving patients with few treatment options. The vaccine is designed to cause a patient’s immune system to attack the cancer cells and could become an effective new treatment that will help these patients live longer.

“Our mission is funding game-changing research to accelerate victory over cancer and save lives,” shared Susanna Greer, PhD, chief scientific officer of the V Foundation. “These four tremendous Dana-Farber investigators illustrate our commitment to funding the best and brightest scientists because today’s cancer research is tomorrow’s victory.”

jetpack-related-posts.title: Damon Runyon invests in promising early career scientists
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Damon Runyon Cancer Research Foundation has awarded more than $3.2 million in grants to nine early career investigators at Dana-Farber, including Mounica Vallurupalli, MD, who was named the foundation’s first Damon Runyon-David M. Livingston, MD, Physician-Scientist.

jetpack-related-posts.title: V Foundation spurs pivotal research aimed at new epigenetic therapies
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The V Foundation is spurring Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s efforts to eradicate difficult-to-treat cancers through recent grants totaling $1.6 million awarded to two Dana-Farber investigators who aim to develop novel treatments known as epigenetic therapies.

jetpack-related-posts.title: V Foundation grants power colorectal cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The V Foundation for Cancer Research once again demonstrated its remarkable generosity and commitment to advancing cancer research at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute by awarding $1.4 million in grants to two exceptional investigators.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Gray Foundation empowers team science against BRCA-mutated cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Philanthropy has transformative power to address society’s intractable challenges. The Gray Foundation is committed to this goal and, with two grants totaling nearly $6 million, is harnessing this power for good through The Dana-Farber Campaign.

jetpack-related-posts.title: V Foundation boosts pediatric AML research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The V Foundation is taking aim at acute myeloid leukemia in children with a grant that will enhance Dana-Farber's search for more effective and durable treatments.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Damon Runyon Cancer Research Foundation invests in tomorrow’s discoveries
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber received over $3,156,000 in grants from the Damon Runyon Cancer Research Foundation in 2024 supporting 10 physician-scientists and researchers.

title.rendered: Over $1 million raised from 2023 Palm Beach Annual Appeal

content.rendered:
Summer 2023
By Samantha Eisenberg
Photography by Capehart Photography

Each year, the Palm Beach community generously comes together to raise funds for Dana-Farber. For the 2023 annual Palm Beach fundraising initiative, Palm Beach donors contributed over $1 million to provide access to revolutionary science and extraordinary patient care that change standards of care around the world.

The Palm Beach Appeal provides flexible funds that help Dana-Farber advance early stage research, speed new drugs into clinical trials, recruit and retain top talent, and ensure that all patients receive the full measure of our Total Patient Care.

“Many of us have experienced Dana-Farber’s excellence firsthand, while others have been alongside a loved one through their cancer journey,” says Phyllis Krock, Dana-Farber Trustee and Palm Beach Annual Appeal chairperson. “Our supporters in Palm Beach are proud to come together to support groundbreaking cancer research that can help save lives beyond our community.”

title.rendered: Gift accelerates new treatment possibilities for neuroendocrine tumors

content.rendered:
Summer 2023
By Cyrena Musset
Photography by Sam Ogden

An anonymous donor first became acquainted with Dana-Farber Cancer Institute in 2021 through their desire to support the fundraising efforts of a friend who is a patient at the Young-Onset Colorectal Cancer Center led by Kimmie Ng, MD, MPH. When the donor’s niece was later diagnosed with a pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor (NET), they knew exactly where to turn. Dr. Ng introduced the donor to Jennifer Chan, MD, MPH, director of the Neuroendocrine and Carcinoid Tumor Program and clinical director of the Gastrointestinal Cancer Center at Dana-Farber. 

The donor was deeply impressed by Chan’s broad knowledge about advances and limitations of current therapy options for neuroendocrine tumors and was eager to be involved in their niece’s care. Inspired by Chan’s work, the donor made a generous gift of $1,000,000 to fund a two-year project led by Chan and Eliezer Van Allen, MD, who is chief of the Division of Population Sciences at Dana-Farber. Van Allen’s lab focuses on computational cancer genomics—the application of new molecular technologies to advance precision cancer medicine and curb resistance to cancer therapeutics using advances in artificial intelligence. Together, Chan and Van Allen wish to learn as much as possible about the immunological microenvironment of NETs, which they hope will lay the framework for developing new immune-based therapies for this disease.  

NETs, particularly pancreatic NETs, are a rare form of cancer that often goes underfunded, so donor support is crucial to make advances in patient care. Thanks to this gift, Chan and Van Allen will use single-cell RNA sequencing approaches on the tumor cells and the immune cells in order to better understand the immune microenvironment of NETs. They further aim to identify mechanisms to augment the immune response with the ultimate goal of developing new immunotherapeutic or vaccine approaches to treat this rare cancer.

“We are very grateful for the support this donor has provided for this crucial research,” Chan said. “We are hopeful that this project will bring us one step closer to providing effective, lasting treatments for this rare disease,” added Van Allen.

“In my experience, great things likely happen when the head meets the heart,” the donor said. “By the head, I mean brilliant ideas and fortitude and by the heart, I mean simply good, caring people. I would tell my fellow donors that at Dana-Farber I frequently feel the head indeed meets the heart.”

title.rendered: Novel clinical trial in pancreatic cancer bolstered by $1 million gift

content.rendered:
Summer 2023
By Colleen Sullivan

John Byrnes is a self-proclaimed “satisfied customer.” Diagnosed with stage IV pancreatic cancer in 2015, John is grateful for each and every day his Dana-Farber care team has given him.

Pancreatic cancer is challenging to treat in its later stages, and also very difficult to catch at an earlier, more treatable stage. Knowing the odds, both John and his wife, Mollie, knew that they needed to go to “the best of the best” for a second opinion. They needed to go to Dana-Farber.

John’s treatment plan included an experimental drug offered in a clinical trial. And while he would not describe his experience as comfortable or an easy road, he and Mollie are grateful that he has survived and lived a very fulfilling seven years—many more years than the original prognosis he was given before coming to Dana-Farber.

“I’m a satisfied customer, and I knew I could trust my team,” said John. “Dana-Farber has A+ people. Every person who touched us makes us feel taken care of, from the receptionist, to the cafeteria workers, to the phlebotomist, to the nurses and doctors.”

One of the most comforting aspects of Dana-Farber for John was his doctors’ willingness to listen and give him options. He and Mollie have expressed their gratitude over the years by giving to Dana-Farber programs that help patients navigate their cancer—including patient assistance, the Blum Family Resource Center Van, and the Hale Family Center for Pancreatic Cancer Research.

Now most recently, the Byrneses have made a very generous gift of $1 million to support clinical research under the direction of John’s doctor, Kimberly Perez, MD.

“We’re motivated to help diagnose earlier, prolong life, and eventually eradicate this dreadful disease,” said Mollie.

With this funding, Perez has launched a clinical trial to test a new combination therapy for patients with localized pancreatic cancer—early stage cancer that has not yet spread to other organs. Perez’s Hale Center colleague Stephanie Dougan, PhD, recently discovered that introducing an inhibitor on the TGF-beta pathway, which is involved in many cellular functions, boosted the efficacy of the chemotherapy used for pancreatic cancer.  The Byrneses’ gift will allow Perez to study the blood and other tissue samples from patients on the trial to understand how this new therapy alters the tumor biology, which will shed light on why some patients respond and others become resistant to the therapy.  

“This clinical trial marks the first bench-to-bedside translational study to be carried out entirely within the Hale Center—a triumph of collaborative science,” said Perez. “By leading clinical trials, we can change how patients with pancreatic cancer are treated across the globe. We’re so grateful for John and Mollie’s generous support.”

jetpack-related-posts.title: Lustgarten grant accelerates therapeutic discovery in pancreatic cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Lustgarten Foundation is the largest private funder of pancreatic cancer research in the world, funding preeminent pancreatic cancer researchers, driving the pursuit of bold and innovative science toward earlier detection and better treatments, and transforming pancreatic cancer into a curable disease.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Doron Broman
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Doron Broman, a Miami-based real estate developer and stage IV pancreatic cancer patient, has given $150,000 to support research in pancreatic cancer under the direction of Kimmie Ng, MD, MPH. Broman came to Dana-Farber in 2015 with only months to live, but under the treatment of Ng, has defied the…

img.alt_text: A doctor and patient smile for a photo

jetpack-related-posts.title: Leon and Leslie Asadoorian
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Leon and Leslie Asadoorian gave $100,000 to advance gastrointestinal cancer research under the direction of Brian Wolpin, MD, MPH, the Robert T. and Judith B. Hale Chair in Pancreatic Cancer at Dana-Farber. Their support will help expand Wolpin’s team of clinical trial experts, enabling them to increase patient enrollment and…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Promises for Purple
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In 2010, shortly after being diagnosed with pancreatic cancer and with encouragement from her two sons, Claire Muollo organized the first Promises for Purple Pancreatic Cancer Awareness 5K Walk in Braintree, Mass.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Campaign: Stopping cancer before it starts
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Dana-Farber Campaign dramatically advanced the prevention, early detection, and interception of cancers on a wide variety of fronts.

img.alt_text: Researchers at work in the Centers for Early Detection and Interception.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Lustgarten Foundation invests $1.5 million to bring promising immunotherapy to patients with pancreatic cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: When the Lustgarten Foundation was founded in 1998, fewer than 10 principal investigators across the U.S. had a primary focus on pancreatic cancer.

title.rendered: Oetgen Family invests in early detection and intervention for myeloma

content.rendered:
Summer 2023
By Lucy Klemarczyk
Photography by Marc Piasecki/Getty Images

Dana-Farber has launched a revolution in myeloma care, thanks to the power of precision medicine, genomics, immunotherapy, and philanthropy. Over the past 20 years, patient lifespan after diagnosis has increased three to five times, and Dana-Farber’s researchers have led the way in pioneering the new treatments that have improved the outlook for patients. The Institute’s reputation for excellence in myeloma research and care reaches far outside of the Greater Boston area and captured the interest of Maggie and Stephen Oetgen in California.

Building on the Institute’s unparalleled expertise, Irene Ghobrial, MD, director of the Center for Prevention of Progression (CPOP) and the Lavine Family Chair for Preventative Cancer Therapies at Dana-Farber, aims to detect myeloma in its earliest stages and intercept it.

Myeloma is preceded by precursor conditions that sometimes progress swiftly without showing symptoms. Although thousands of patients are diagnosed annually with such precursor conditions, there are no effective therapies to prevent disease progression and most patients do not receive treatment until they develop cancer.

Ghobrial and her team of researchers and clinicians are working to change the “watch and wait” standard of care by investigating treatments that can interrupt the disease in its earliest, pre-cancerous stages. For example, Dana-Farber is the first site in the world to offer teclistamab, a novel therapy, to patients with precursors in a clinical trial, and is also the first site in the world to secure approval for a CAR T-cell therapy clinical trial for precursors under Ghobrial’s leadership.

“We have been thrilled to do all that we can to support Dr. Ghobrial’s many efforts both now, and into the future.”

Stephen and Maggie Oetgen

To advance this pioneering work, the Oetgens established the Oetgen Immunotherapy Fund at Dana-Farber with a generous $1 million investment. The Oetgen Immunotherapy Fund will accelerate novel immunotherapies from late-stage development in the lab to clinical trials, where they can be delivered to patients for the first time. The Oetgens shared their motivation for this magnificent gift: “After meeting Irene Ghobrial, and hearing about all of the tremendous work that she and her team at Dana Farber are doing to prevent cancer through the use of cutting-edge therapies which harness the powerful capabilities of her patients’ own immune systems, we have been thrilled to do all that we can to support her many efforts both now, and into the future.”

Ghobrial remarked, “Thanks to the support of the Oetgens, I can accelerate progress and meet our critical goals of identifying who is at risk of developing myeloma and why, and to deliver precision medicine to patients with precursor conditions with a focus on immunotherapy.”

jetpack-related-posts.title: International Myeloma Society
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s Mohammad Rashidian, PhD, received a $250,000 Translational Research Award from the International Myeloma Society and the Paula and Rodger Riney Foundation. This support will advance his innovative work to combat disease relapse in multiple myeloma patients following CAR T-cell therapy.

jetpack-related-posts.title: IMS grants drive innovative multiple myeloma research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The International Myeloma Society (IMS) recently awarded three Dana-Farber scientists grants totaling $525,000 to promote research on the blood cancer multiple myeloma.

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Paula and Rodger Riney Foundation sustains momentum in multiple myeloma research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Multiple myeloma treatments have significantly improved over the past two decades, thanks in part to the driving engine of transformational philanthropy.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Unrestricted support: A powerful vote of confidence
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Dana-Farber Campaign is a catalyst for giving at every level, including through the Defy Cancer Fund, and has inspired tremendous unrestricted support from our generous philanthropic community.

img.alt_text: An image of a scientist looking through a test tube (image has blue overlay)

jetpack-related-posts.title: Gift honors late wife and supports multiple myeloma research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Kenneth Nirenstein remembers his late wife, Harriet, as wise, elegant, and graceful. After Harriet’s passing, seeking a way to keep her memory alive while also making a difference to others, Kenneth made a gift of $100,000 to establish the Harriet Shapiro Nirenstein Fund for Multiple Myeloma Research at Dana-Farber.

img.alt_text: A photo of a couple in front of an ocean

jetpack-related-posts.title: Smith Family support inspires others to help speed multiple myeloma research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Paul Richardson has found an important partner in Robert and Dana Smith, who recently made a $3 million gift to continue supporting his advanced MM clinical trials research.

title.rendered: Defeating advanced and aggressive kidney cancers

content.rendered:
Summer 2023
By Kathy Clute

The Kidney Cancer Association (KCA) has made $650,000 in grants to three Dana-Farber researchers who are unlocking the molecular mechanisms of a disease that will be diagnosed in nearly 82,000 U.S. residents this year and claim the lives of more than 14,000.

The Texas-based organization is dedicated to finding a cure for kidney cancer by promoting scientific advances through an annual grant program and scientific symposiums. At the same time, it provides education and resources for patients and their caregivers. Since 2002, KCA has given nearly $1.4 million to Dana-Farber.

Toni Choueiri, MD, director of the Institute’s Kidney Cancer Center and of the Lank Center for Genitourinary Oncology, and the Jerome and Nancy Kohlberg Professor of Medicine, received KCA’s Advanced Discovery Award. His pioneering work has already led to FDA approval for an immune checkpoint inhibitor that dramatically extends disease-free survival in patients who have undergone surgery for clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC). However, the disease almost always recurs in patients who have metastatic ccRCC. With the KCA award, Choueiri and his team are focused on thwarting advanced disease with cytokine-induced memory-like (CIML) natural killer (NK) cells.

KCA also honored Yufei Wang, PhD, and Srinivas Viswanathan, MD, PhD, with Trailblazer Awards, which go to promising early to mid-career investigators who are undertaking innovative research. Wang is genetically engineering CAR T cells, a highly effective form of immunotherapy in bloodborne cancers, to attack the cancer cells in the solid tumors found in kidney cancer.

Viswanathan is focusing on translocation renal cell carcinoma (tRCC), a rare but aggressive subtype of kidney cancer for which there is no targeted treatment. Only five percent of adult kidney cancers are of this type, but it accounts for up to 50 percent of such cancers in children. It is also notable for occurring in younger, female patients and responds poorly to therapies that are effective in ccRCC.

Gretchen E. Vaughan, president and CEO of the Kidney Cancer Association, noted that nearly 600,000 Americans are living with kidney and renal pelvis cancer. “Dana-Farber is bringing us closer to the day when these patients have effective treatments and, ultimately, a cure,” she said.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Accelerating progress for adenoid cystic carcinoma
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Nearly two decades ago, Marnie Kaufman was diagnosed with adenoid cystic carcinoma (ACC), a rare type of cancer most commonly arising in the salivary glands. Shortly thereafter, she and her husband, Jeff, established the Adenoid Cystic Carcinoma Research Foundation.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Hyundai Hope On Wheels invests in innovative treatments for children
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Since 1998, Hyundai Motor America and Hyundai Hope On Wheels have represented a powerful engine of support for pediatric cancer research.

img.alt_text: Hyundai Hope on Wheels 25 years logo

jetpack-related-posts.title: AACR grants support sarcoma, renal cell carcinoma, and cancer biology research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The American Association for Cancer Research (AACR) recently awarded $580,000 to three Dana-Farber physician-scientists who are investigating new methods of prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of various types of cancers. As the first cancer research organization dedicated to preventing and curing cancer, AACR is a long-standing partner in Dana-Farber’s mission to…

jetpack-related-posts.title: Breast Cancer Research Foundation grants more than $4 million to speed Dana-Farber research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Building on past support, BCRF recently made grants totaling more than $4 million to 12 physician-scientists at Dana-Farber.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Breast cancer patient inspires endowed fund at Dana-Farber
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Suzanne Michels Obenshain was 42 years old and living in Switzerland with her husband and three young children when she was diagnosed with stage IV triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC).

img.alt_text: Suzanne Michels Obenshain with her children on a ski trip

jetpack-related-posts.title: Rallying to defy pediatric cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Bolstering Dana-Farber’s mission to defy cancer, Rally Foundation for Childhood Cancer Research made grants totaling $850,000 in 2023 to help drive much-needed progress in pediatric oncology research.

title.rendered: Red Sox name 2023 Jimmy Fund Captain

content.rendered:
Summer 2023
By Molly McHale
Photography by Maddie Malhotra/Boston Red Sox

Boston Red Sox pitcher Garrett Whitlock, has been named Jimmy Fund Captain for the 2023 baseball season. Whitlock will be an ambassador for the Jimmy Fund’s 75th anniversary and will help to support and promote Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and the Jimmy Fund’s mission to defy cancer. The Red Sox have partnered with the Jimmy Fund since 1953, the longest and most successful charitable partnership in professional sports, and as Jimmy Fund Captain, Whitlock will continue this tradition.

“Like all players in MLB, I am aware of the strong partnership and rich history between the Red Sox organization, the players, and the Jimmy Fund. I am honored to be asked to serve as this year’s Jimmy Fund Captain. I look forward to meeting patients and their families and helping to raise awareness and funds for all the amazing work that is being done at Dana-Farber,” said Whitlock.

As Jimmy Fund Captain, Whitlock will attend fundraising events, visit patients, build support and raise funds for cancer care and research at Dana-Farber. Funds raised through the Jimmy Fund support The Dana-Farber Campaign, the Institute’s ambitious, multi-year fundraising effort to prevent, treat, and defy cancer through revolutionary science, extraordinary care, exceptional expertise, and essential opportunities—saving more lives than ever before.

“I look forward to meeting patients and their families and helping to raise awareness and funds for all the amazing work that is being done at Dana-Farber.”

Garrett Whitlock, Jimmy Fund Captain

“We are thrilled to have Garrett Whitlock as our Jimmy Fund Captain this year,” said Larry Lucchino, Chairman of the Jimmy Fund, Trustee of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, Chairman/Principal Owner of the Worcester Red Sox, and President/CEO Emeritus of the Boston Red Sox. “Garrett’s involvement, and support of the Jimmy Fund and the Red Sox community, continues a long line of talented and selfless players who have served as ambassadors to support the Jimmy Fund’s important mission of defying cancer.  Thank you, Garrett.”

Past Jimmy Fund Captains include Nathan Eovaldi, Mitch Moreland, Brock Holt, Pablo Sandoval, Will Middlebrooks, David Ross, Jarrod Saltalamacchia, Daniel Bard, Clay Buchholz, and Tim Wakefield.

content.rendered:
Summer 2023
By Colleen Sullivan
Photography by Pan-Mass Challenge

On Feb. 4, hundreds of riders assembled at Fenway Park’s 521 Overlook venue for the PMC Winter Cycle, an annual indoor spinning event to raise money for Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. This year, riders raised more than $530,000, 100% of which will go directly to supporting cancer research and patient care at the Institute.

Record breaking temperatures reaching minus 10 degrees didn’t stop these fundraisers from venturing out to work up a sweat for cancer research and care. Even Wally the Green Monster made an appearance to rally the crowd as they rode through six 45-minute sessions led by top Boston-area cycling instructors.

The Winter Cycle kicked off the 2023 fundraising season for the Pan-Mass Challenge, the annual bike-a-thon that is the nation’s most successful athletic fundraiser and the Institute’s largest single contributor.

jetpack-related-posts.title: PMC Winter Cycle
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The one-of-a-kind PMC Winter Cycle was held at Fenway Park on March 9, with hundreds of riders participating to support patient care and research at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute.

img.alt_text: Cyclists participating in the PMC Winter Cycle at Fenway Park

jetpack-related-posts.title: Pan-Mass Challenge celebrates PMC Pedal Partners from the Jimmy Fund Clinic at Fenway Park
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On May 17, dozens of PMC Pedal Partners—pediatric patients from the Jimmy Fund Clinic at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute paired with PMC riders and teams—gathered at The 521 Overlook at Fenway Park to meet the cyclists participating in the 46th PMC on Aug. 2 and 3.

img.alt_text: A family of four at Fenway Park

jetpack-related-posts.title: 2025 PMC Winter Cycle
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC), the nation’s single most successful athletic fundraiser and Dana-Farber’s largest single contributor, kicked off its 2025 fundraising year at the 10th PMC Winter Cycle on Feb. 1 at Fenway Park.

img.alt_text: Bikers on stationary bikes at the PMC Winter Cycle event

jetpack-related-posts.title: PMC Check Presentation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC) community came together at Rochambeau Restaurant in Boston on Sunday, Nov. 2, for the 2025 PMC Check Presentation.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Pan-Mass Challenge raises record $72 million to bring cures closer by the mile
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On long journeys, landmarks and milestones show us where we are and how far we’ve come. Since 1980, the Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC), the beloved bike-a-thon and the nation’s most successful athletic fundraiser, has seen plenty of both.

img.alt_text: Pan-Mass Challenge riders along the route

jetpack-related-posts.title: One in a billion: Pan-Mass Challenge surpasses $1 billion fundraising milestone
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In 2024, the Pan-Mass Challenge had a banner year, as the organization generated a record gift of $75 million and surpassed an extraordinary $1.047 billion in lifetime fundraising since its founding in 1980.

title.rendered: Prado gift supports access for the underprivileged

content.rendered:
Summer 2023
By Robbie Merritt

Institute Trustee Gary Prado and his wife, Darlene Prado, have established The Prado Family Impact Fund at Dana-Farber to honor Gary’s late mother, Gisela Herrera, and Darlene’s mother, Minerva Tejeda, who were treated at Dana-Farber.

For the Prados, the fund is the perfect tribute to their mothers, both immigrants from the Dominican Republic who worked tirelessly to build lives of opportunity for their families. Now, Gary and Darlene are helping families who are struggling to do the same, while also fighting cancer. The Prado Family Impact Fund will improve health care access for underprivileged communities of color by directly supporting the Patient Assistance Program at Dana-Farber, which helps reduce barriers to high-quality cancer care through financial support and assistance with transportation and lodging.

“Dana-Farber is a place that treats all its patients with the utmost care and attention, regardless of social or economic status. That is something that truly resonates with us, as people from underprivileged families,” says Darlene. “I saw firsthand the dignity with which my mom and Gary’s mom were treated by Dana-Farber, and we see The Prado Family Impact Fund as an investment in Dana-Farber’s commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion.”

“Dana-Farber is a place that treats all its patients with the utmost care and attention, regardless of social or economic status.”

Darlene Prado

title.rendered: Tuli gift plans for today and tomorrow

content.rendered:
Summer 2023
By Colleen Sullivan
Photography by David Fox Photography

When asked why he became involved with Dana-Farber, Institute Trustee Sushil Tuli tells the story of his late wife, Rita, and her treatment for colon cancer at another hospital. Rita spent many hours in an infusion center and, while she was treated well, Tuli wished she had a more comforting place to spend those hours.

“If Dana-Farber can save somebody’s life, they’re going to save it. There is no better institution than this.”

Sushil Tuli, Dana-Farber Trustee

After Rita passed away, Tuli joined the Institute’s Board and later made a gift that named an infusion bay in Rita’s honor at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute – Chestnut Hill. The space is warmly lit, features many windows, and is a welcoming place that Tuli feels will bring comfort to all patients receiving treatment there.

Tuli also established a charitable gift annuity (CGA), which allows donors to make a gift now and receive lifetime income for themselves or a beneficiary, as well as potential tax benefits. Tuli felt this was the perfect way to give, as it enables planning for Dana-Farber’s future while at the same time planning for his family’s. With this gift, Tuli became a member of the Dana-Farber Society.

“I’m a true spokesperson for Dana-Farber,” said Tuli. “If Dana-Farber can save somebody’s life, they’re going to save it. There is no better institution than this.”

jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: For over three decades, the compassionate community in Palm Beach, Florida, has provided generous support for Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s lifesaving mission to conquer cancer in adults and children—not only in Boston and Palm Beach, but also across the country and around the world.

jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Palm Beach community once again demonstrated remarkable generosity by raising over $1.31 million to support Dana-Farber Cancer Institute through their Palm Beach Annual appeal.

title.rendered: Levin gift honors Lee Nadler, MD

content.rendered:
Summer 2023
By Michael Quinn

How do you thank the doctor who saved your loved one’s life? You help other physicians do the same for their patients.

Ronnie Levin and her family recently made a gift of $100,000 through the Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC) to establish the Levin/Nadler Award, which will support the work of exceptional early career investigators at Dana-Farber. This annual award is named for Lee Nadler, MD, senior vice president of experimental medicine and the PMC Chair at Dana-Farber, who courageously treated Ronnie’s husband, Larry, for large cell, high-grade, non-Hodgkin lymphoma in 1986.

“We are honored to support talented young investigators that embody the creativity and courage of Dr. Nadler, who literally cured Larry’s cancer and changed the course of our lives.”

Ronnie Levin

Known for going the extra mile for his patients, Nadler put Larry on an experimental therapy that worked when all other treatments failed. Larry lived another 35 years and formed a strong bond with Nadler, who in 1991 first encouraged Larry to ride in the PMC—the annual bike-a-thon that is the nation’s most successful athletic fundraiser and the Institute’s largest single contributor. Larry and Ronnie did so 11 times, including four rides with their daughter, Kim, providing early “Living Proof” of the impact of Nadler and the PMC. The Levin Family hopes that today’s trailblazing physician-scientists will be inspired by Nadler’s example and pursue bold research that helps other patients survive cancer. Ronnie said, “We are honored to support talented young investigators that embody the creativity and courage of Dr. Nadler, who literally cured Larry’s cancer and changed the course of our lives.”

jetpack-related-posts.title: Gift continues donor’s legacy by supporting gastrointestinal research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Throughout her life, Ilene Beal was dedicated to hard work and breaking down barriers. She became a female pioneer in the Boston banking world and was a valued mentor for other women in the industry.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Celebrating the PMC’s $1 billion milestone
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In January, Dana-Farber leadership welcomed dedicated members of the Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC) community for a special event celebrating their success raising more than $1 billion since 1980 and the transformative impact these funds have had on the lives of our patients.

jetpack-related-posts.title: New England Shoe Foreman & Superintendents Association
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The New England Shoe Foremen & Superintendents Association has made a gift of $100,000 to help support new and advanced treatments for pediatric cancer patients. The research and care supported by the association are intended to improve the survival and overall quality of life for these patients and their families.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Physician pioneer in palliative care establishes a research fellowship
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In 2001, Janet L. Abrahm, MD, joined Dana-Farber Cancer Institute as a palliative care physician, becoming a pivotal force in founding and nurturing the Adult Palliative Care Program—a move that created a sea change in how Dana-Farber cares for patients with cancer and brought much-deserved attention and recognition to the field.

content.rendered:
Summer 2023
By Kayla Carcone

In 2010, shortly after being diagnosed with pancreatic cancer and with encouragement from her two sons, Claire Muollo organized the first Promises for Purple Pancreatic Cancer Awareness 5K Walk in Braintree, Mass. Since then, the event has raised over $271,000 for pancreatic cancer research at Dana-Farber. Claire passed away in 2014, but her legacy lives on in every advance made and each person clad in purple at the annual walk in November.

“Raising awareness and bringing people together was my mom’s original intention for this walk,” said Robert Muollo, event organizer and Claire’s oldest son. “She’d be proud to know how much her efforts have transformed care, but also how it continues to bring our family together in a meaningful way.”

“Promises for Purple has helped to propel real momentum in early detection and prevention efforts, as our team works to identify biomarkers and increase genetic testing, and I have greatly enjoyed walking with my family at this event for more than 10 years,” said Brian Wolpin, MD, MPH, director of the Gastrointestinal Cancer Center and the Robert T. and Judith B. Hale Chair in Pancreatic Cancer at Dana-Farber. “The Muollo Family and the event organizers are a special group, and we are extremely appreciative of their dedication to this cause in honor of Claire.”

Claire Muollo embodied faith, positivity, and humor in the face of her obstacles. As a patient, she would “grade” Wolpin at each appointment. Today, with all the tireless work and breakthroughs made in pursuit of a pancreatic cancer-free future, Robert Muollo said, “I know she would give him a very well-deserved A+.”

jetpack-related-posts.title: Novel clinical trial in pancreatic cancer bolstered by $1 million gift
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: John Byrnes is a self-proclaimed “satisfied customer.” Diagnosed with stage IV pancreatic cancer in 2015, John is grateful for each and every day his Dana-Farber care team has given him.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Kendall Family prioritizes innovation in pancreatic cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In cancer research, hope can be realized in how we innovate. Inventive clinical trials can lead to novel approaches and new, accessible medicines that ultimately bring better outcomes to patients.

img.alt_text: Rich and Beth Kendall with their family.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Lustgarten grant accelerates therapeutic discovery in pancreatic cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Lustgarten Foundation is the largest private funder of pancreatic cancer research in the world, funding preeminent pancreatic cancer researchers, driving the pursuit of bold and innovative science toward earlier detection and better treatments, and transforming pancreatic cancer into a curable disease.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Lustgarten Foundation invests $1.5 million to bring promising immunotherapy to patients with pancreatic cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: When the Lustgarten Foundation was founded in 1998, fewer than 10 principal investigators across the U.S. had a primary focus on pancreatic cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Ilene Beal Charitable Foundation gift focuses on cancer interception
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A $1.25 million gift to Dana-Farber from the Ilene Beal Charitable Foundation supports research focused on ways pancreatic cancer might be detected—and intercepted—before it can be seen on CT scans or other imaging modalities.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Mulligan Family Fundraiser
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Mulligan Family organized a birthday fundraiser for Dana-Farber in honor of their loved one, Patrick. They raised over $15,000 to help James Cleary, MD, PhD, standardize screening options and uncover more effective treatments for pancreatic cancer.

content.rendered:
Summer 2023
By Colleen Sullivan

In March, the Awards and Milestones Reception recognized participants in the 2022 Boston Marathon® Jimmy Fund Walk presented by Hyundai who went above and beyond, including Alumni Walker of the Year Barb Sirvis. Barb walks in honor and memory of the 950+ names that she handwrites on the back of her shirt every year. Also honored at the ceremony were: First-Time Team Captain of the Year Anita Rodriguez; First-Time Walker of the Year Anya Rhodes; Alumni Team Captain of the Year Julie Wilson; Volunteer of the Year Venu Nareddy; and Extra Mile Award recipient Carole Hauke. Lifetime Fundraising Awards were given to Team Owen’s Army, who surpassed $1 million in fundraising, and Team Kroot, who surpassed $500,000; and individual walkers Ed Gardella, Janis Moriarty, Amy Schwartz Messina, and Janet Schwartz.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Walkers go the extra mile for the Jimmy Fund
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The annual Awards and Milestones Reception recognized participants of the 2023 Boston Marathon® Jimmy Fund Walk presented by Hyundai who went above and beyond.

img.alt_text: Zach’s Pack Jimmy Fund Walk fundraising group

jetpack-related-posts.title: Walkers go the extra mile for the Jimmy Fund
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The annual Awards and Milestones Reception recognized participants of the 2024 Jimmy Fund Walk presented by Hyundai who went above and beyond in helping to raise nearly $9.4 million.

img.alt_text: Five Jimmy Fund Walk participants wearing Jimmy Fund Walk gear

jetpack-related-posts.title: Boston Marathon® Jimmy Fund Walk celebrates 35 years of inspiration and impact
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Last fall, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute patients, families, and supporters joined forces to defy cancer at the 35th annual Boston Marathon® Jimmy Fund Walk presented by Hyundai, which raises the most money of any single-day walk in the nation.

img.alt_text: A group of Jimmy Fund Walk participants pose for a photo in their Walk t-shirts

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jimmy Fund Walk steps into record-breaking year with over $11.2 million raised
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On a sunny Sunday in October 2025, the Jimmy Fund Walk presented by Hyundai, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s signature fundraising event, crossed more than just the finish line at Boston Common.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Back on course with the Boston Marathon® Jimmy Fund Walk
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: For 34 years, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute supporters have come together for a day of inspiration and hope at the Boston Marathon® Jimmy Fund Walk presented by Hyundai, raising lifesaving funds to defy cancer for patients everywhere.

img.alt_text: Walkers and volunteers on the route of the Boston Marathon Jimmy Fund Walk

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jimmy Fund Walk defies cancer with $9.4 million
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Thanks to more than 8,400 participants, the 2024 Jimmy Fund Walk surpassed $185 million in funds raised over 37 years for Dana-Farber's lifesaving mission.

img.alt_text: Three people pose for a photo, with one person holding a framed t-shirt with signatures

content.rendered:
Spring 2023
By Lori Dougherty

The Dana-Farber Campaign is an ambitious, multi-year fundraising effort to change the future of cancer research and care—the largest in the Institute’s history and one of the largest ever in the U.S. focused solely on cancer. Our community of support is crucial to this effort.

Establishing an endowment is a powerful way to support The Dana-Farber Campaign. The annual distribution from an invested endowment provides long-term, budget-relieving funds for Dana-Farber’s clinical, research, or educational programs, or for faculty or nursing positions, enabling the Institute to attract and retain the brightest minds in the field. Endowments can be established with a wide range of tax-efficient gifts, from cash and checks to donor-advised funds, IRAs, stocks, securities, and other financial assets. Opportunities are available at a variety of giving levels (see below) and are payable over five years.

Gifts to create an endowment accelerate the Institute’s strategic priorities by supporting the most promising scientific discoveries, our nursing and medical professionals, and continued support of our unique Dana-Farber culture—helping us prevent, treat, and Defy Cancer for patients everywhere.

Endowed Giving Opportunities

To learn more, visit DefyCancer.org.

excerpt.rendered: Establishing an endowment is a powerful way to support The Dana-Farber Campaign.

content.rendered:
Spring 2023

Dear Friends,

We are thrilled to unveil the Spring 2023 issue of Impact—the first of our newly redesigned magazine and website! As the celebration of the 75th anniversary of Dana-Farber draws to a close, the launch of this magazine and website, DanaFarberImpact.org, reflects our guiding philosophy at Dana-Farber: a commitment to always evolving while honoring our strong, historic foundation and the people who helped build it. 

In launching this website we have strived to make the stories from our community of supporters more accessible and informative. In the upper right corner of each page is a drop-down that lets you choose the language in which you want to view the site, and a search box to help you find topics of interest. Each page also features links at the bottom to facilitate sharing with others in your network, or with family and friends. And we have taken care throughout the website to employ best practices for text, colors, mobile functionality, and other features to improve access for all. 

This launch also coincides with the Jimmy Fund’s 75th anniversary, an incredible milestone which we will be celebrating throughout the year with all of you. Over the past 75 years, support through the Jimmy Fund has enabled Dana-Farber to push boundaries in cancer care and research—reducing the rate of mortality from cancer, strategically growing our physical footprint to reach more patients, recruiting and retaining world-class physicians, nurses, and scientists, and supporting patients through treatment into survivorship. 

With that in mind, we are very excited to move into the next 75 years together with you, our dedicated partners. On DanaFarberImpact.org you will read about the special collaborations advancing our ambitious research agenda, the shared purpose of our Jimmy Fund community, and a selection of very special gifts provided in support of The Dana-Farber Campaign priorities. With spring around the corner, we look forward to longer days, more light, and a fresh presentation of the generosity and commitment of Dana-Farber donors and friends.  

With gratitude,

Melany N. Duval
Senior Vice President and Chief Philanthropy Officer

excerpt.rendered: We are thrilled to unveil the Spring 2023 issue of Impact—the first of our newly redesigned magazine and website!

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Message from Melany Duval
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: When I first stepped into my role at Dana-Farber in 2019, I was immediately struck by the endless compassion and dedication of the people around me.

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Message from Melany Duval
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Because of your support for The Dana-Farber Campaign, our impact and growth will expand by an order of magnitude we have only begun to imagine.

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Message from Melany Duval
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Thanks to the tenacity and generosity of our entire community over the last seven years of The Dana-Farber Campaign, we are defying cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Message from Melany Duval
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: One of the things that makes Dana-Farber such a special place is our emphasis on teamwork.

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Message from Melany Duval
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dear friends, Every day our philanthropic community supports a relentless commitment to possibilities in cancer care at Dana-Farber—and that gives me hope.

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Message from Melany Duval
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Over the past seven years, The Dana-Farber Campaign has enabled incredible progress at the Institute, the effects of which ripple out to help patients around the world.

Spring 2023
By Colleen Sullivan
Photography by Sam Ogden

Margaret and Michael Bayer gave $100,000 to establish The Bayer Family Research Fund. The fund aims to accelerate discoveries into safer, more effective and durable treatments for patients facing Waldenström’s macroglobulinemia, a rare form of blood cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Michael and Margaret Kerr
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Michael and Margaret Kerr established the Kerr Family Fund for Translational Research at Dana-Farber with a $100,000 gift in 2023. The fund will be directed by James Cleary, MD, PhD, whom the couple laud for his compassionate patient care.

img.alt_text: A photo of two people outside on a balcony

jetpack-related-posts.title: Margaret and Michael Kerr
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Margaret and Michael Kerr’s generous gift of $100,000 to the Kerr Family Fund for Translational Research supports the groundbreaking work of James Cleary, MD, PhD, at Dana-Farber. Their contribution will help advance innovative treatment approaches for gastrointestinal cancers, underscoring their vital role in transforming patient care.

img.alt_text: Various tubes and other lab equipment

jetpack-related-posts.title: Robert Cummins
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Robert Cummins gave $100,000 to establish The Deborah Cummins Waldenström’s Memorial Fund in honor of his late wife. Cummins’ investment is enabling a team at Dana-Farber’s Bing Center for Waldenström’s Macroglobulinemia to lead clinical trials that are pivotal in the development of more durable, effective treatments.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Children’s Cancer Research Fund
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Children’s Cancer Research Fund awarded their Emerging Scientist Award to Dana-Farber pediatric oncologist Emily Heikamp, MD, PhD, MSc. The grant of $100,000 will support Heikamp’s work in uncovering therapeutic vulnerabilities in the NU98-r gene, which could lead to safer and more effective treatments for children with relapsed acute myeloid leukemia.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Beerman Family Fund fuels next-generation approach to cancer vaccines
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Gift may help speed production, reduce cost, and increase personalization of cancer vaccines to be more effective in many types of cancers.

img.alt_text: Two people outside in front of trees and bushes

jetpack-related-posts.title: Barbara and Arnold Barron
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Barbara and Arnold Barron gave $100,000 to support lung cancer research under the direction of Michael Rabin, MD. The couple has supported the work of Rabin and Dana-Farber for many years, this gift marking their latest commitment to spur advancements in durable treatments for lung cancer patients at Dana-Farber and…

title.rendered: Boston Red Sox Jimmy Fund Award

content.rendered:
Spring 2023
By Colleen Sullivan
Photography by Maddie Malhotra/Boston Red Sox

The 2022 Boston Red Sox Jimmy Fund Award—the Jimmy Fund’s highest honor—was presented to John Berardi (second from right), program director of Jimmy Fund Little League presented by Franklin Sports, which rallies thousands of youth baseball and softball players each summer to fundraise for the Jimmy Fund in their communities and has raised over $6 million for Dana-Farber since 1986.

jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan

jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Boston Red Sox pitcher, Garrett Whitlock, has been named Jimmy Fund Captain for the 2023 baseball season.

img.alt_text: Jimmy Fund Captain Garrett Whitlock in the Fenway dugout with pediatric patient Lily

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jimmy Fund Little League
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Jimmy Fund Little League presented by Franklin Sports raised $281,332 in 2023 for cancer research and care at Dana-Farber. Every year, Little League baseball and softball players in New England raise vital funds for the Jimmy Fund during this summer league, making a significant impact in the fight against cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jimmy Fund Little League
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Jimmy Fund Little League presented by Franklin Sports raised more than $272,000 for Dana-Farber in its 39th season. New England’s young baseball and softball players extended their Little League® seasons to take a swing at cancer by raising vital funds for cancer research and care at Dana-Farber.

content.rendered:
Spring 2023
By Colleen Sullivan

Breast Cancer Alliance awarded $125,000 to Dana-Farber to support research into the features of the tumor microenvironment that result in metastatic triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). This work will improve researchers’ knowledge of the behavior of TNBC and may help identify patients who are more likely to benefit from treatments such as immunotherapy.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Breast cancer patient inspires endowed fund at Dana-Farber
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Suzanne Michels Obenshain was 42 years old and living in Switzerland with her husband and three young children when she was diagnosed with stage IV triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC).

img.alt_text: Suzanne Michels Obenshain with her children on a ski trip

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dana-Farber joins with Parker Institute for Cancer Immunotherapy to accelerate cures for the world’s gravest cancers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Dana-Farber has partnered with the Parker Institute for Cancer Immunotherapy (PICI), the leading network of immuno-oncology expertise in the world, as a member of the PICI Network with a goal of better understanding the tumor microenvironment across cancer types and translating these basic discoveries into impactful cancer immunotherapies for patients.

img.alt_text: T cells (white) lining for an attack on human triple-negative breast cancer cells (red and yellow)

jetpack-related-posts.title: METAvivor advances metastatic breast cancer research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: METAvivor has awarded three grants totaling $850,000 to advance metastatic breast cancer research at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Susan G. Komen funds research into new breast cancer treatments
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In its mission to eradicate breast cancer, Susan G. Komen has invested nearly $1.1 billion in research since its founding in 1982. In 2023, Komen continued a longstanding partnership with Dana-Farber by awarding $2.3 million in new grants to Dana-Farber faculty members.

jetpack-related-posts.title: New grants advance key research across multiple disease areas
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Longtime Dana-Farber supporter Conquer Cancer,® the ASCO Foundation, recently awarded $1.45 million to support seven researchers pursuing projects in a wide range of disease areas.

jetpack-related-posts.title: A Legacy of Leadership and Hope: The Elaine and Eduardo Saverin Foundation’s generational commitment to patients with metastatic breast cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Elaine and Eduardo Saverin Foundation has made an extraordinary $20 million grant to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute to accelerate research and care for people living with stage IV breast cancer.

Spring 2023
By Colleen Sullivan
Photography by Michael Blanchard

Fred and Michele Brettschneider made a commitment of $250,000 to support a clinical trial network for Waldenström’s macroglobulinemia and advance all clinical research for this rare form of blood cancer within the Bing Center for Waldenström’s Macroglobulinemia.

jetpack-related-posts.title: New multi-institution network to drive progress in rare blood cancer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Colleen Sullivan
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The International Waldenstrom’s Macroglobulinemia Foundation (IWMF) recently committed $2.5 million to support a new multi-institutional network for clinical and research programs dedicated to Waldenström’s macroglobulinemia (WM).

jetpack-related-posts.title: IWMF awards $1.4 million to Dana-Farber investigators, fueling Waldenstrom’s Macroglobulinemia research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: For more than two decades, the International Waldenstrom’s Macroglobulinemia Foundation (IWMF) has been a vital philanthropic partner to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, accelerating research into Waldenstrom’s macroglobulinemia (WM), a rare, slow-growing blood cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Luigi and Patrizia D’Amato
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Luigi and Patrizia D’Amato made a gift of $100,000 to support research within the Bing Center for Waldenström’s Macroglobulinemia at Dana-Farber. The center is the largest in the world dedicated to the study of Waldenström’s macroglobulinemia, a slow-growing type of blood cancer that most often forms in the bone marrow.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Margaret and Michael Bayer
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Margaret and Michael Bayer gave $100,000 to establish The Bayer Family Research Fund. The fund aims to accelerate discoveries into safer, more effective and durable treatments for patients facing Waldenström’s macroglobulinemia, a rare form of blood cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Ellice and David Vittor
jetpack-related-posts.author: Hannah White
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With their gift of $150,000, Ellice and David Vittor established the Vittor Family Research Fund to advance research by Steven Treon, MD, PhD, and the Bing Center for Waldenström’s Macroglobulinemia. The Bing Center is the largest center in the world dedicated to researching this rare blood cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Robert Cummins
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Robert Cummins gave $100,000 to establish The Deborah Cummins Waldenström’s Memorial Fund in honor of his late wife. Cummins’ investment is enabling a team at Dana-Farber’s Bing Center for Waldenström’s Macroglobulinemia to lead clinical trials that are pivotal in the development of more durable, effective treatments.

By Colleen Sullivan

The Burlingame Foundation gave $300,000 to provide support for patient navigation through the Cancer Care Equity Program (CCEP). Patient navigation involves supporting and assisting patients through the complexities of treatment—a key component of the CCEP’s effort to address disparities in cancer care.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Synergy Fund at The Boston Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Synergy Fund at The Boston Foundation gave $200,000 in support of the Cancer Care Equity Program (CCEP) at Dana-Farber. With these funds, the CCEP team will continue to address disparities in health care for underserved patient populations and pursue equitable care for every cancer patient.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Expanding equitable access to critical care
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Last year, the National Breast Cancer Foundation (NBCF) generously provided $155,000 to support Dana-Farber’s inclusion, diversity, and equity work to ensure equitable health outcomes for all.

img.alt_text: National Breast Cancer Foundation, Inc. Logo

jetpack-related-posts.title: Expanding patient navigation through philanthropy
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With donor support through The Dana-Farber Campaign, the Institute piloted a new community-facing patient navigation program in 2021 to assist patients with transportation, language services, insurance, nutrition, and other social and economic concerns that may be barriers to care.

img.alt_text: Patient Navigator Marlene Escobar and Vice President of Community Health Magnolia Contreras are pictured outside of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute

jetpack-related-posts.title: National Foundation for Cancer Research
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The National Foundation for Cancer Research awarded over $300,000 to Dana-Farber’s Kornelia Polyak, MD, PhD, to advance research in metastatic breast cancer. This funding will support her work in treatment resistance in HER2+ breast cancer brain metastases and ultimately help transform the landscape of patient care.

img.alt_text: National Foundation for Cancer Research logo

jetpack-related-posts.title: St. Baldrick’s Foundation
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: St. Baldrick’s Foundation has awarded grants totaling $395,000 to fund pediatric cancer research by Institute researchers Rahela Aziz-Bose, MD, and Jun Qi, PhD. The grants will support their research to better understand and tackle barriers to nutrition for childhood cancer survivors and identify novel targets for pediatric brain tumors and…

jetpack-related-posts.title: The Dana-Farber Campaign: Closing the equity gap in cancer care
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Funds from The Dana-Farber Campaign allow us to expand access to underserved populations and improve research to reduce disparities in treatment outcomes.

img.alt_text: Patient Navigator Judy Thyme, MSPH (left), assists patient Carle Price with her medications.

Spring 2023
By Colleen Sullivan

The annual Cross-Check Cancer Women’s Hockey Tournament raised more than $40,000 in 2022, a new record, to support the Adult Survivorship Program in the Perini Family Survivors’ Center at Dana-Farber. The tournament draws 38 teams and more than 470 participants from 11 states to raise funds to ensure a healthy quality of life after cancer.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Swim Across America
jetpack-related-posts.author: Lori Dougherty
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Swim Across America raised $250,000 in 2024 to benefit Dana-Farber’s Perini Family Survivors’ Center. Since 1996, the Boston Open Water Swim has united swimmers of all ages and abilities, raising over $3.5 million in total to support vital survivorship research at Dana-Farber and continuing to “Make Waves Against Cancer.”

jetpack-related-posts.title: Expect Miracles Foundation raises record $1.25 million
jetpack-related-posts.author: Dana-Farber Impact
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A dedicated supporter of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute for more than 28 years, Expect Miracles Foundation marked a record-breaking year in 2022 by raising $1.25 million in support of the Robert and Renée Belfer Center for Applied Cancer Science at Dana-Farber.

img.alt_text: Expect Miracles Foundation with large check for Dana-Farber

jetpack-related-posts.title: Rybacki Memorial surpasses $1 million

jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Thirty years ago, 16 golfers in the first Rybacki Memorial Golf Tournament raised $1,200 for Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. In 2022, 150 golfers raised more than $145,000

content.rendered:
Spring 2023
By Colleen Sullivan
Photography by Justin Knight

In October, Dana-Farber supporters and leaders gathered for the annual Dana-Farber Cancer Institute Presidential Symposium. Attendees received firsthand updates on the State of the Institute, advances and opportunities in prevention and early detection, the impact of philanthropy on advancing research, and Dana-Farber’s world-renowned hematology/oncology fellowship program. Pictured are fellowship program graduates and panelists (from left): Ann LaCasce, MD, MMSc, program director and the Fellowship Program in Hematology/Oncology Chair at Dana-Farber; Levi Garraway, MD, PhD, EVP, head of global product development and chief medical officer, Roche and Genentech; and Nadine McCleary, MD, MPH, medical director, Patient Reported Data Program at Dana-Farber.

content.rendered:
Spring 2023
By Colleen Sullivan

In September, the inaugural David Liposarcoma Research Initiative International Scientific Symposium was held at Dana-Farber. The symposium included the unveiling of a plaque commemorating the generous pledge from the Rossy Foundation that, through The Rossy Foundation Fund at KBF Canada, established the David Liposarcoma Research Initiative under the direction of George Demetri, MD, director of the Sarcoma Center, senior vice president of Experimental Therapeutics, and the Quick Family Chair in Medical Oncology at Dana-Farber. Pictured (from left) at the event: George Demetri, MD, with Nicole Solimini, PhD, and Greg David of the Rossy Foundation.

excerpt.rendered: In September, the inaugural David Liposarcoma Research Initiative International Scientific Symposium was held at Dana-Farber. The symposium included the unveiling of a plaque commemorating the generous pledge from the Rossy Foundation that, through The Rossy Foundation Fund at KBF Canada, established the David Liposarcoma Research Initiative under the direction of George Demetri, MD, director of the Sarcoma Center, senior vice president of Experimental Therapeutics, and the Quick Family Chair in Medical Oncology at Dana-Farber. Pictured (from left) at the event: George Demetri, MD, with Nicole Solimini, PhD, and Greg David of the Rossy Foundation.
